children.title: Convex Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Convex lower approximations considered relative to a specified domain.

children.title: Underestimator Applicability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Closed, bounded, unbounded, continuous, and lower-semicontinuous settings for underestimation.

children.title: Domain Regimes
children.top_down_role: Closed, bounded, plus unbounded domains relevant to convex underestimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes global, restricted-domain, and partition-local convex underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a real vector space, let \(\Omega\subseteq X\), and let \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). For a convex set \(D\subseteq\Omega\), a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(D\) is a convex function \(g:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \(g(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). The underestimator is global relative to \(\Omega\) when \(\Omega\) is convex and \(D=\Omega\), restricted-domain when \(D\) is a prescribed convex relaxation region, and partition-local when its validity is confined to a convex cell \(D_j\subseteq D\). If \(C\subseteq D\) is convex, then \(g|_C\) is a convex underestimator of \(f|_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex lower model may be valid on an entire convex objective domain, on a prescribed convex relaxation region, or only on a convex partition cell; restricting it to a smaller convex set preserves validity.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real vector space and \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
\(D\subseteq\Omega\) and every restriction or partition cell under consideration are convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every convex \(C\subseteq D\), \(g|_C\le f|_C\), and \(g|_C\) remains convex.

notation.meaning: domain on which underestimation is required

children.title: Regularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Continuous plus lower-semicontinuous settings for underestimator construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity inherited from convexity, with boundary continuity treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex with nonempty relative interior, and let \(g:D\to\mathbb R\) be convex. Then \(g\) is continuous, and locally Lipschitz, on \(\operatorname{ri}D\). Thus a finite convex underestimator requires no separate interior continuity assumption. Continuity at \(\operatorname{rbd}D\), differentiability, strict convexity, and strong convexity are additional regularity regimes and do not follow from convexity alone. If a closed lower model is required, its epigraph must be closed, equivalently \(g\) must be lower semicontinuous relative to \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite convex underestimators are continuous and locally Lipschitz in the relative interior; boundary continuity, differentiability, and stronger curvature require separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is continuous and locally Lipschitz on \(\operatorname{ri}D\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-interior continuity and local-Lipschitz claims are standard and mathematically plausible, but the cited locator is a section on convex sets and does not specifically locate these function-regularity results or the closed-epigraph equivalence. A theorem or section on continuity of convex functions and closed convex functions is required.

children.title: Domain-Boundary Behavior
children.top_down_role: Boundary-sensitive changes in validity, closure, or tightness.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Boundary Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary values need not be determined by finite convex interior behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(D=[0,1]\), define \(g(0)=1\) and \(g(x)=0\) for \(0<x\le1\). Then \(g\) is finite and convex on \(D\), but it is not lower semicontinuous at \(0\), since \(g(0)>\liminf_{x\downarrow0}g(x)=0\). Consequently, finite convexity guarantees regularity only on the relative interior and does not prevent an upward boundary jump. Replacing a convex underestimator by its lower-semicontinuous hull can repair closedness, but the resulting boundary values may be strictly smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite convex function can jump upward at a domain boundary, so closedness or boundary continuity must be imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\) is convex but not lower semicontinuous at \(0\).

notation.meaning: right lower limit at the boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and fits the failure-boundary container, but the cited convex-sets locator does not specifically support boundary discontinuity of finite convex functions or lower-semicontinuous closure. Supply a locator addressing boundary behavior or this example.

children.title: Underestimator Contact Geometry
children.top_down_role: Touching sets, interpolation structure, and boundary contact as sources of tightness.

children.title: Contact Sets
children.top_down_role: Locations where an underestimator touches the original function.

knowledge_statements.title: Contact Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality locus between an objective and its convex underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(g:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(g\le f\) on \(D\). The contact set of \(g\) with \(f\) over \(D\) is
\[\mathcal C_D(f,g):=\{x\in D:g(x)=f(x)<+\infty\}.\]
For \(x\in D\setminus\mathcal C_D(f,g)\) with finite function values, the nonnegative gap \(f(x)-g(x)\) is strict. The contact set need not be convex, even when \(g\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The contact set consists precisely of finite domain points where the underestimator equals the original objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal C_D(f,g)\) exactly when \(g(x)=f(x)<+\infty\).

notation.meaning: contact set of the objective and underestimator
underestimation gap where both values are finite

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117

children.title: Interpolation Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric patterns induced by exact matching at selected domain points.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolation Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes affine interpolation by a convex underestimator on a simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_0,\ldots,v_k\in D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be affinely independent contact points of a convex underestimator \(g\le f\), and let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_k\}\). The model interpolates the vertex data affinely on \(S\) precisely when, for every \(x=\sum_{i=0}^k\lambda_i v_i\) with \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i=0}^k\lambda_i=1\),
\[g(x)=\sum_{i=0}^k\lambda_i f(v_i).\]
Convexity alone yields only \(g(x)\le\sum_{i=0}^k\lambda_i f(v_i)\); equality is the additional interpolation condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a simplex of contact points, affine interpolation means the lower model equals the barycentric interpolation of the objective’s vertex values.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is convex on a convex set \(D\) and satisfies \(g\le f\).
\(v_0,\ldots,v_k\) are affinely independent members of \(\mathcal C_D(f,g)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g|_S\) is affine with the prescribed vertex values exactly when the displayed barycentric equality holds.

notation.meaning: simplex generated by the contact points

children.title: Boundary Contact
children.top_down_role: Tightness associated with contact on domain boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Contact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contact restricted to the relative boundary of the relaxation domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(g\le f\) be a convex underestimator on \(D\). Its boundary-contact set is
\[\mathcal B_D(f,g):=\mathcal C_D(f,g)\cap\operatorname{rbd}D.\]
The underestimator has complete boundary contact when \(g(x)=f(x)<+\infty\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{rbd}D\), and partial boundary contact when \(\mathcal B_D(f,g)\) is a proper nonempty subset of \(\operatorname{rbd}D\). Boundary contact is distinct from continuity at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary contact is equality between the objective and lower model at relative-boundary points; it may be complete, partial, or absent.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is convex on \(D\) and satisfies \(g\le f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_D(f,g)=\mathcal C_D(f,g)\cap\operatorname{rbd}D\).

notation.meaning: relative boundary of the relaxation domain

children.title: Underestimator Dominance Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Dominance, maximal underestimators, and comparison over common domains.

children.title: Dominance Ordering
children.top_down_role: Pointwise strength relations among underestimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise order among valid convex underestimators on one domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(f:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and let \(\mathcal U_D(f)\) be the set of convex functions \(g:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \(g\le f\) on \(D\). For \(g_1,g_2\in\mathcal U_D(f)\), define \(g_1\preceq_D g_2\) when \(g_1(x)\le g_2(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Then \(\preceq_D\) is a partial order modulo pointwise equality. If \(g_1\preceq_D g_2\), the model \(g_2\) dominates \(g_1\) and supplies an objective lower bound at least as large on every feasible subset of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One convex underestimator dominates another when it is pointwise no smaller throughout their shared validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_1\preceq_D g_2\) if and only if \(g_1(x)\le g_2(x)\) for all \(x\in D\).

notation.meaning: valid convex underestimators of the objective on the domain
pointwise dominance order on the common domain

children.title: Maximal Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Underestimators that admit no strictly stronger member in the relevant class.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates order-maximal underestimators from a greatest convex underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal U_D(f),\preceq_D)\) be the pointwise ordered family of admissible convex underestimators. An element \(g\in\mathcal U_D(f)\) is maximal if \(g\preceq_D h\) for \(h\in\mathcal U_D(f)\) implies \(h=g\) pointwise. It is greatest if \(h\preceq_D g\) for every \(h\in\mathcal U_D(f)\). A greatest element, when it exists, is unique and maximal; a maximal element need not dominate every other underestimator. For proper extended-real objectives, the greatest closed convex underestimator is the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope whenever that envelope is proper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal lower model admits no strict pointwise improvement; a greatest model dominates all admissible lower models and is therefore unique.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U_D(f)\) is ordered by pointwise dominance.
For the envelope assertion, the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of \(f\) on \(D\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every greatest underestimator is uniquely determined and maximal, whereas maximality alone does not imply greatestness.

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order-theoretic maximal and greatest definitions are correct, but the assertion identifying the greatest closed convex underestimator with the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope depends on domain, extension, closure, and properness conventions not established here. A precise convex-envelope theorem locator is required.

children.title: Common-Domain Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Strength comparisons restricted to shared domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Domain Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for comparing lower models constructed on different domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D_1\cup D_2\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and for \(i\in\{1,2\}\) let \(g_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(g_i(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D_i\). A pointwise dominance comparison requires a nonempty common set \(C\subseteq D_1\cap D_2\). On \(C\), \(g_1\) dominates \(g_2\) precisely when \(g_2(x)\le g_1(x)\) for every \(x\in C\). If \(D_1\cap D_2=\varnothing\), no nonempty common-domain comparison exists. Comparing only \(\inf_{x\in C}g_1(x)\) and \(\inf_{x\in C}g_2(x)\) is weaker than pointwise dominance and does not establish an ordering of the restricted functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower models built on different domains can be ordered after restriction to a nonempty shared subset; comparing only their minimum values is weaker than pointwise dominance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_2|_C\preceq_C g_1|_C\) exactly when \(g_2(x)\le g_1(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).

notation.meaning: validity domain of the corresponding underestimator
restriction of a lower model to the common domain

children.title: Convex Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Problem-level relaxations combining objective underestimation with convex outer descriptions of constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value ordering for convex underestimating relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orders the original MINLP value, the exact penalty-envelope relaxation, the componentwise convex-envelope relaxation, and an arbitrary componentwise convex-underestimator relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the box-constrained MINLP \(M\), let \(R_P^{**}\) minimize over the box the convex envelope of a penalty function \(P\) that is exact for \(M\); let \(R_h^{**}\) replace each objective and constraint function by its convex envelope on the box; and let \(\breve R\) use arbitrary convex underestimators. Then \[\operatorname{val}(M)=\operatorname{val}(R_P^{**})\ge \operatorname{val}(R_h^{**})\ge \operatorname{val}(\breve R).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the penalty formulation is exact, the MINLP and the convex envelope of that penalty have the same optimal value. This value dominates the componentwise convex-envelope bound, which in turn dominates the bound from any selected componentwise convex underestimators.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is an exact penalty function for }M\text{ on }X=[\underline x,\bar x].
\breve h_i\text{ is convex on }X\text{ and }\breve h_i(x)\le h_i(x)\quad(\forall x\in X,\ i=0,\ldots,m).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{val}(M)=\operatorname{val}(R_P^{**})\ge\operatorname{val}(R_h^{**})\ge\operatorname{val}(\breve R).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex relaxation and its lower-bound property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers same-variable and lifted convex relaxations of minimization problems, including a sufficient construction using convex underestimators and a convex outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\), a same-variable relaxation \(\inf_{x\in\widehat S}\widehat f(x)\) satisfies \(S\subseteq\widehat S\) and \(\widehat f(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in S\). It is a convex relaxation if \(\widehat S\) is convex and \(\widehat f\) is convex on \(\widehat S\). More generally, \(\inf_{z\in Z}\bar f(z)\) is a lifted convex relaxation when \(Z\) is convex, \(\bar f\) is convex, and for every \(x\in S\) there exists \(z\in Z\) such that \(\bar f(z)\le f(x)\). In either case, the relaxation value is a lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\). If \(S=\{x:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), convex functions \(\widehat f\) and \(\widehat g_i\) satisfying \(\widehat f(x)\le f(x)\) and \(\widehat g_i(x)\le g_i(x)\) for all \(x\in S\) give the sufficient construction \(\widehat S=\{x:\widehat g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), for which \(S\subseteq\widehat S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A same-variable convex relaxation uses a convex feasible superset and a convex objective that underestimates the original objective at every original feasible point. A lifted relaxation may instead associate each original feasible point with a point in another convex set having no larger objective value. Either construction gives a lower bound on the original infimum. Convex underestimators of the objective and constraints provide one sufficient same-variable construction, but convex outer approximations need not be produced this way.
assumptions_latex: S\subseteq\widehat S,\qquad \widehat f(x)\le f(x)\quad\forall x\in S
\widehat S\text{ is convex and }\widehat f\text{ is convex on }\widehat S
\text{or }Z\text{ is convex},\ \bar f\text{ is convex, and }\forall x\in S\;\exists z\in Z:\bar f(z)\le f(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in\widehat S}\widehat f(x)\le\inf_{x\in S}f(x),\qquad\text{or in the lifted case}\qquad\inf_{z\in Z}\bar f(z)\le\inf_{x\in S}f(x)

source_evidence.locator: Lower Bounds / 4.1. Introduction / Definition 4.1

knowledge_statements.title: Convex relaxation and its lower-bound property

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex underestimating relaxation of a box-constrained MINLP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines componentwise convex-underestimator relaxations and records the associated envelope ordering and conditional exact-penalty-envelope result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[\underline x,\bar x]\) and consider \(\min\{h_0(x):h_i(x)\le 0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ x\in X,\ x_B\text{ binary}\}\). If each \(\breve h_i\) is convex on \(X\) and \(\breve h_i(x)\le h_i(x)\) for all \(x\in X\), replacing \(h_i\) by \(\breve h_i\) and dropping integrality defines a convex underestimating relaxation \(\breve R\). Replacing each \(h_i\) by its convex envelope \(h_{i,X}^{**}\) defines the strongest relaxation within this componentwise-underestimator class, denoted \(R_h^{**}\), and \(\operatorname{val}(\breve R)\le \operatorname{val}(R_h^{**})\). If the penalty function \(P\) described in the source is exact on \(X\), then its convex-envelope problem \(R_P^{**}=\min_{x\in X}P_X^{**}(x)\) is exact: \(\operatorname{val}(M)=\operatorname{val}(R_P^{**})\) and \(\operatorname{sol}(R_P^{**})=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{sol}(M))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex functions that underestimate every model function on the box yield a convex relaxation when integrality is removed. Componentwise convex envelopes give the strongest relaxation of this particular form. Conditionally, if the source's penalty function is exact, minimizing its convex envelope preserves the MINLP optimal value and has the convex hull of the original minimizers as its solution set.
assumptions_latex: \breve h_i\text{ is convex on }X\text{ and }\breve h_i(x)\le h_i(x)\quad(\forall x\in X,\ i=0,\ldots,m).
P\text{ is exact on }X\text{ for the penalty-envelope exactness conclusion}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{val}(\breve R)\le\operatorname{val}(R_h^{**});\qquad P\text{ exact}\Longrightarrow\operatorname{val}(M)=\operatorname{val}(R_P^{**}),\quad\operatorname{sol}(R_P^{**})=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{sol}(M)).

children.title: Objective-Function Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Lower models for nonconvex objectives over a prescribed relaxation domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Function Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower-model relaxation of a minimization objective over a prescribed domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F\subseteq D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). If \(g:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex and satisfies \(g(x)\le f(x)\) on \(D\), the objective-function relaxation is
\[p_g=\inf\{g(x):x\in R\},\]
where \(R\supseteq F\) is convex and contained in \(D\). It obeys \(p_g\le p^*\). Equality holds whenever an optimizer \(x^*\in F\) exists, belongs to the contact set of \(f\) and \(g\), and minimizes \(g\) over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a convex underestimator over a convex superset of the feasible set produces a valid lower bound on the original minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is convex on \(D\) and satisfies \(g\le f\) there.

notation.meaning: convex relaxation of the feasible set

children.title: Constraint-Function Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Paired lower and upper models used to outer-approximate nonlinear constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Function Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer relaxation using lower models for inequalities and paired bounds for equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the original feasible set be \(F=\{x\in D:c_i(x)\le0,\ i\in I;\ h_j(x)=0,\ j\in E\}\). For each inequality choose a convex underestimator \(\underline c_i\le c_i\). For each equality choose a convex underestimator \(\underline h_j\le h_j\) and a concave overestimator \(\overline h_j\ge h_j\). Then
\[R=\{x\in D:\underline c_i(x)\le0,\ i\in I;\ \underline h_j(x)\le0\le\overline h_j(x),\ j\in E\}\]
contains \(F\). If \(D\) is convex, the lower models are convex, and the upper models are concave, then \(R\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating inequality functions and bracketing equality functions yields a convex outer approximation containing every originally feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\underline c_i,\underline h_j\) is convex and valid below its target; each \(\overline h_j\) is concave and valid above its target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq R\), and \(R\) is convex.

source_refs.locator: 9.3 Problems with General Nonconvex Objective Function p. 190

source_witnesses.locator: 9.3 Problems with General Nonconvex Objective Function p. 190

children.title: Joint Formulation Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Convexification that retains relationships among objectives, constraints, and shared expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Formulation Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted convex relaxation preserving shared-expression relationships across the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an optimization formulation uses shared nonlinear expressions \(w_k=\phi_k(x)\) in its objective and constraints. Introduce one lifted variable \(w_k\) for each shared expression and replace its graph by a convex set \(G_k\) satisfying
\[\{(x,w_k):x\in D,\ w_k=\phi_k(x)\}\subseteq G_k.\]
Replacing every occurrence of \(\phi_k(x)\) by the same \(w_k\), and imposing all sets \(G_k\) together with convex relaxations of the remaining relations, gives a joint convex feasible set \(R\) containing every lifted original feasible point. Minimizing a convex lower objective model over \(R\) yields a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint relaxation lifts shared expressions once and convexifies their coupled graph relations, preserving dependencies while containing the original formulation.
assumptions_latex: Each graph relaxation \(G_k\) is convex and contains the corresponding restricted graph.
All occurrences of a shared expression use the same lifted variable.
The relaxed objective is a valid convex lower model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) contains the lifted original feasible set, and its relaxed minimum is no greater than the original minimum.

notation.meaning: lifted variable for a shared nonlinear expression
convex outer approximation of a restricted expression graph

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum preservation by the convex envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States equality of minimum values and inclusion of the original minimizers among the envelope minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be convex and compact, let f:S\to\mathbb{R} be lower semicontinuous, and let \phi be the convex envelope of f on S. Writing f^*=\min_{x\in S}f(x), one has \min_{x\in S}\phi(x)=f^*. Moreover, \{y\in S:f(y)=f^*\}\subseteq\{y\in S:\phi(y)=f^*\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact convex set, a lower-semicontinuous function and its convex envelope have the same minimum value, and every minimizer of the original function is also an envelope minimizer; the envelope may have additional minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \phi\text{ is the convex envelope of }f\text{ on }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in S}f(x)=\min_{x\in S}\phi(x)=f^*,\qquad \{y\in S:f(y)=f^*\}\subseteq\{y\in S:\phi(y)=f^*\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex envelope as the greatest convex underestimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the convex envelope of a lower-semicontinuous function on a nonempty convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be convex, and let f:S\to\mathbb{R} be lower semicontinuous. The convex envelope of f on S is a function \phi:S\to\mathbb{R} such that: (i) \phi is convex on S; (ii) \phi(x)\le f(x) for every x\in S; and (iii) every convex function h:S\to\mathbb{R} satisfying h(x)\le f(x) for all x\in S also satisfies h(x)\le\phi(x) for all x\in S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope is the greatest convex function lying below the given function everywhere on the domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi\text{ is convex on }S,\quad \phi\le f\text{ on }S,\quad\text{and}\quad \forall h\text{ convex on }S,\ h\le f\Rightarrow h\le\phi

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Geometry for Triangle Convex Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Under the preceding triangle curvature conditions, characterizes an attaining support in representation (4.5) according to the number of strictly convex edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}\), and let \(\ell\) be the number of edges along which \(f\) is strictly convex. For \(x\in T\setminus G(f,X)\), the minimum in (4.5) is attained as follows: for \(\ell=0\), by \(x_i=v_i\), \(i=1,2,3\); for \(\ell=1\), by the vertex opposite the strictly convex edge and a point on that edge; for \(\ell=2\), by one point on each of the two strictly convex edges; and for \(\ell=3\), by one point on one of the two edges selected in Condition 3 and one point on the third edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated triangle curvature regime, an attaining support for the convex-envelope representation uses the three vertices when no edge is strictly convex. When one, two, or three edges are strictly convex, it uses two boundary points in the edge configurations specified by the lemma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{cases}\ell=0:&x_i=v_i,\ i=1,2,3,\\\ell=1:&\text{one opposite vertex and one point on the strictly convex edge},\\\ell=2:&\text{one point on each strictly convex edge},\\\ell=3:&\text{one point on a selected Condition-3 edge and one on the third edge}.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representations of the convex envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-envelope representations under the surrounding nonempty-domain, lower-semicontinuity, and 1-coercivity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[(\operatorname{co}f)(x)=\sup\{g(x):g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is convex and }g\leq f\},\] \[(\operatorname{co}f)(x)=\sup\{\langle s,x\rangle-b:\langle s,y\rangle-b\leq f(y)\ \forall y\in\mathbb{R}^n\},\] and \[(\operatorname{co}f)(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}\alpha_i f(x_i):\alpha\in\Delta_{n+1},\ x_i\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ \sum_{i=1}^{n+1}\alpha_i x_i=x\right\}.\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{co}f)=\operatorname{co}(\operatorname{epi}f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope is the greatest convex minorant of f. It is also the supremum of all affine minorants and has a finite convex-combination representation; its epigraph is the convex hull of the epigraph of f.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{co}f\text{ has the convex-minorant, affine-minorant, finite-mixture, and epigraph convex-hull representations stated above.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-preservation property of the convex envelope over the convex hull of a compact domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex envelope on a convex set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition conditional on the existence of a greatest real-valued convex minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq H\) be nonempty and convex. A function \(h_M:M\to\mathbb R\) is the convex envelope of \(h\) over \(M\) if it is convex, satisfies \(h_M(x)\le h(x)\) for all \(x\in M\), and every convex \(q:M\to\mathbb R\) with \(q(x)\le h(x)\) for all \(x\in M\) satisfies \(q(x)\le h_M(x)\) for all \(x\in M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex underestimators and the convex envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise definition of convex underestimators and their supremal envelope over a set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:S\to\mathbb R\), let \(\mathcal U(f,S):=\{\xi:S\to\mathbb R:\xi\text{ is convex and }\xi(x)\le f(x)\ \forall x\in S\}\). Every \(\mu\in\mathcal U(f,S)\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\) over \(S\). The convex envelope is \(\operatorname{vex}_S[f](x):=\sup\{\mu(x):\mu\in\mathcal U(f,S)\}\) for \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex underestimator is a convex function lying pointwise below the given function. The convex envelope is the pointwise supremum of all such underestimators.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal U(f,S)=\{\xi:S\to\mathbb R:\xi\text{ is convex and }\xi\le f\text{ on }S\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{vex}_S[f](x)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal U(f,S)}\mu(x)\quad\forall x\in S

children.top_down_role: Envelope geometry expressed through epigraph convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Convex-Hull Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex envelope represented by convexifying the extended epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and extend \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(F=f+\delta_C\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Assume \(F\) is proper and bounded below by an affine function. The greatest lower-semicontinuous convex function majorized by \(F\), denoted \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F\), satisfies
\[\operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}F).\]
Consequently, the closed convex envelope of \(f\) on \(C\) is obtained by taking the closed convex hull of its extended epigraph and reading its lower boundary over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed convex envelope is the lower boundary of the closed convex hull of the function's extended epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}F)\).

notation.meaning: Indicator equal to zero on C and positive infinity outside C.
Epigraph of the extended-real-valued function F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Envelope via Epigraph Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the convex envelope of a nonconvex function and its restriction to a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be nonconvex. The function determined by \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{conv}g)=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}g)\) is the convex envelope of \(g\); it is the largest convex function majorized by \(g\). For \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define \((g\mid C)(x)=g(x)\) when \(x\in C\) and \((g\mid C)(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. The convex envelope of \(g\) over \(C\) is \(\operatorname{conv}(g\mid C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying the epigraph of a nonconvex function yields its convex envelope, the largest convex function lying below it. Over a set C, first extend the function to positive infinity outside C and then take its convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{conv}g)=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}g),\quad \operatorname{conv}g\le g,\quad \operatorname{conv}_C g=\operatorname{conv}(g\mid C).

knowledge_statements.title: Biconjugate Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel biconjugate form of the closed convex envelope in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper function \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) admitting an affine minorant, define
\[F^*(y)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{\langle y,x\rangle-F(x)\},\qquad F^{**}(x)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{\langle y,x\rangle-F^*(y)\}.\]
Then
\[F^{**}=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F,\]
so \(F^{**}\) is the greatest lower-semicontinuous convex minorant of \(F\). For a function specified only on \(C\), apply the formula to \(F=f+\delta_C\) and restrict the result to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fenchel biconjugate of the extended function equals its greatest lower-semicontinuous convex minorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{**}=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}F\).

notation.meaning: Greatest lower-semicontinuous convex minorant of F.

children.title: Lower-Semicontinuous Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure effects governing the represented lower approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Semicontinuous Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure operation converting a convex envelope into its closed convex counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an extended-real function \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), its lower-semicontinuous closure \(\operatorname{cl}g\) is the function determined by
\[\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}g)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}g),\]
provided the closed epigraph contains no vertical line corresponding to the value \(-\infty\). Equivalently,
\[(\operatorname{cl}g)(x)=\liminf_{z\to x}g(z).\]
If \(g\) is convex and proper, then \(\operatorname{cl}g\) is lower-semicontinuous and convex, satisfies \(\operatorname{cl}g\le g\), and is the greatest lower-semicontinuous function below \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-semicontinuous closure closes the epigraph, equivalently replacing each value by the nearby lower limit.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper and convex for the final convexity assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}g)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}g)\) and \((\operatorname{cl}g)(x)=\liminf_{z\to x}g(z)\).

notation.meaning: Lower limit over points approaching x.

children.title: Closed-Envelope Coincidence
children.top_down_role: Regimes where the closed convex envelope matches the biconjugate representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Envelope Coincidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient compactness and semicontinuity conditions under which closure adds nothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower-semicontinuous. If \(f\) is bounded below by an affine function, then its convex envelope \(g=\operatorname{conv}_C f\) is lower-semicontinuous on \(C\). Hence the ordinary and closed convex envelopes coincide:
\[\operatorname{conv}_C f=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}_C f=(f+\delta_C)^{**}\big|_C.\]
Equivalently, closing the epigraph of the convex envelope introduces no new boundary values over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact convex domain, a proper lower-semicontinuous function has the same ordinary and closed convex envelopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}_C f=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}_C f=(f+\delta_C)^{**}\big|_C\).

notation.meaning: Greatest convex minorant of f on C.
Greatest lower-semicontinuous convex minorant on C.

children.title: Convex-Mixture Representation
children.top_down_role: Finite-support convex combinations and associated support geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Mixture Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise envelope formula using finite-support barycentric decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) admit a convex minorant. Its convex envelope satisfies
\[(\operatorname{conv}_C f)(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i f(x_i):m\in\mathbb{N},\ x_i\in C,\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i x_i=x\right\}.\]
In finite dimension, the infimum may be restricted to mixtures having at most \(n+1\) positive weights. If the infimum is not attained, such mixtures approximate the envelope value arbitrarily closely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope value is the least weighted function value among finite barycentric representations of the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\operatorname{conv}_C f)(x)=\inf\{\sum_i\lambda_i f(x_i):\sum_i\lambda_i x_i=x,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \lambda_i\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: Convex envelope of f relative to C.
Support points of a convex mixture.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Combination Representation of the Convex Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation theorem for convex hulls in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, $\operatorname{conv}E$ consists exactly of all finite convex combinations of points of $E$: \[\operatorname{conv}E=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i x_i:r\in\mathbb{N},\ x_i\in E,\ \lambda_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i=1\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of E is exactly the set of all finite convex combinations of elements of E.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}E=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i x_i:r\in\mathbb{N},\ x_i\in E,\ \lambda_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i=1\right\}.

children.title: Interval Envelopes

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional envelope formula through lower chords on a compact interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}\) with \(\ell<u\), and let \(f:I\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) admit a convex minorant. For every \(x\in I\),
\[(\operatorname{conv}_I f)(x)=\inf\left\{\lambda f(a)+(1-\lambda)f(b):a,b\in I,\ \lambda\in[0,1],\ x=\lambda a+(1-\lambda)b\right\}.\]
Thus each envelope value is determined by the lowest chord value obtainable from two points of the graph; the degenerate choice \(a=b=x\) is allowed. If \(f\) is lower-semicontinuous, the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an interval, the convex envelope is the lowest value supplied by a chord through two graph points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\operatorname{conv}_I f)(x)=\inf\{\lambda f(a)+(1-\lambda)f(b):x=\lambda a+(1-\lambda)b\}\).

notation.meaning: Endpoints of a candidate graph chord.

children.title: Cartesian-Box Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Convex envelopes specialized to multidimensional Cartesian boxes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Box Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex envelopes relative to bounded Cartesian-product domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[B=\prod_{j=1}^{n}[\ell_j,u_j]\subset\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad \ell_j<u_j,\]
and let \(f:B\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). The Cartesian-box convex envelope of \(f\) is the pointwise greatest convex function on \(B\) lying below \(f\):
\[(\operatorname{conv}_B f)(x)=\sup\{g(x):g:B\to(-\infty,+\infty],\ g\text{ is convex},\ g(y)\le f(y)\text{ for all }y\in B\}.\]
Equivalently, it is given by the convex-mixture formula with all support points constrained to \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian-box envelope is the greatest convex underestimator whose domain and mixture support are restricted to the box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}_B f=\sup\{g:g\text{ convex on }B,\ g\le f\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lovász-Extension Characterization of the Hypercube Convex Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives necessary and sufficient conditions for the convex envelope on the unit hypercube to equal the Lovász extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex envelope of $f$ over $[0,1]^n$ is its Lovász extension if and only if $G(f,[0,1]^n)=V([0,1]^n)$ and $f$ is submodular over $V([0,1]^n)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope on the unit hypercube equals the Lovász extension exactly when the relevant generating set is the hypercube vertex set and the function is submodular on that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}_{[0,1]^n}f=f^L\iff\left(G(f,[0,1]^n)=V([0,1]^n)\ \land\ f\text{ is submodular over }V([0,1]^n)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Point Optimal Representation of a Box Convex Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduces an optimal convex-envelope representation to at most two generating points under opposing coordinate-block curvature assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X=\prod_{i=1}^n[l_i,u_i]$. Suppose that $f$ is convex in the remaining $n-1$ variables whenever $x_1$ is fixed and concave in $x_1$ whenever the remaining variables are fixed. If $\mathbf x_1^\star,\ldots,\mathbf x_k^\star\in G(f,X)$, with $k\leq n+1$, are the points of an optimal solution of the mixture problem defining the convex-envelope value at $\mathbf x$, then there exists an optimal solution with $k\leq2$. If $k=2$, then $\mathbf x_1^\star\in F_1$ and $\mathbf x_2^\star\in F_2$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated blockwise convexity and concavity conditions, the convex-envelope value over a box has an optimal representation using at most two generating points; when two are used, they lie in the source-defined sets F1 and F2.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is convex in }(x_2,\ldots,x_n)\text{ whenever }x_1\text{ is fixed}.
f\text{ is concave in }x_1\text{ whenever }(x_2,\ldots,x_n)\text{ are fixed}.
\mathbf x_1^\star,\ldots,\mathbf x_k^\star\in G(f,X),\quad k\leq n+1,\text{ are points in an optimal solution defining the convex-envelope value at }\mathbf x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an optimal solution with }k\leq2;\qquad k=2\implies\mathbf x_1^\star\in F_1\text{ and }\mathbf x_2^\star\in F_2.

source_evidence.locator: Lower Bounds / 4.2. Convex envelopes / Theorem 4.18

children.title: Dimension-Sensitive Box Structure
children.top_down_role: Envelope features that change when passing from intervals to higher-dimensional boxes.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Sensitive Box Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient dimension controls the support size needed for exact box-envelope mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=\prod_{j=1}^{n}[\ell_j,u_j]\) be a nonempty compact box, and let \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\) be lower-semicontinuous. For every \(x\in B\), there exist \(m\le n+1\), points \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in B\), and weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\) such that
\[\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i=1,\qquad x=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i x_i,\qquad (\operatorname{conv}_B f)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i f(x_i).\]
Thus an exact envelope value needs no more than \(n+1\) active support points, although the box itself has \(2^n\) vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In dimension n, an attained box-envelope value requires at most n+1 active support points, despite the box having exponentially many vertices.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty compact Cartesian box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\operatorname{conv}_B f)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i f(x_i)\) for some \(m\le n+1\).

notation.meaning: Number of active mixture support points.
Number of vertices of a nondegenerate n-dimensional box.

children.title: Simplex Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope structure on simplicial domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope representation on a simplex, including the concave-function vertex formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nondegenerate simplex and let \(f:S\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) admit a convex minorant. Its envelope is given by mixtures of at most \(n+1\) points of \(S\). If \(f\) is concave and finite-valued, every \(x\in S\) has unique barycentric coordinates \(x=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\lambda_i(x)v_i\), and
\[(\operatorname{conv}_S f)(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\lambda_i(x)f(v_i).\]
Hence, for concave data, the simplex envelope is the unique affine interpolant of the vertex values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a concave function on a simplex, the convex envelope is the affine interpolation of its vertex values.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite-valued and concave for the vertex formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\operatorname{conv}_S f)(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}\lambda_i(x)f(v_i)\) when \(f\) is concave.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine convex envelope of a concave function on a simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique affine interpolation of vertex values on the simplex's affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}\) be a simplex and let \(f:S\to\mathbb R\) be concave. The convex envelope \(\phi\) of \(f\) on \(S\) is the unique affine function \(A:\operatorname{aff}(S)\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
A(v_i)=f(v_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Thus \(\phi(x)=A(x)\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a simplex, the convex envelope of a concave function is the unique affine function on the simplex's affine hull that interpolates all vertex values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi=A\text{ on }S,\quad A(v_i)=f(v_i)\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,n

children.title: Polytope Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope structure on general polyhedral domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Polytope Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-mixture formula for concave functions on compact polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_N\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty compact polytope, and let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave. Then its convex envelope is
\[(\operatorname{conv}_P f)(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i f(v_i):\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i v_i=x\right\}.\]
An optimal representation can be chosen with at most \(n+1\) positive weights. The resulting envelope is convex and polyhedral, even when \(f\) is not polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For concave data on a polytope, the convex envelope minimizes interpolated vertex values over all vertex decompositions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\operatorname{conv}_P f)(x)=\min\{\sum_i\lambda_i f(v_i):\sum_i\lambda_i v_i=x,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \lambda_i\ge0\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal-Affine-Dependency Criterion for a Triangulated Polytope Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when the piecewise-affine vertex interpolant associated with a triangulation is the convex envelope on a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a polytope with $V(X)=\{\mathbf v_1,\ldots,\mathbf v_k\}$, and suppose $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ admits a vertex polyhedral convex envelope over $X$. For a triangulation $T$ of $X$, define $g_T(\mathbf x)=L_{f,\Delta}(\mathbf x)$ when $\mathbf x\in\Delta\in T$, where $L_{f,\Delta}$ affinely interpolates $f$ at the vertices of $\Delta$. Then $g_T$ is the convex envelope of $f$ over $X$ if and only if, for every minimal affine dependency $\lambda$ satisfying $\{\mathbf v_i:i\in P(\lambda)\}\subseteq\Delta''\in T$ and $\{\mathbf v_i:i\in N(\lambda)\}\subseteq\Delta'\notin T$, one has $\sum_{i\in P(\lambda)}\lambda_i f(\mathbf v_i)\leq-\sum_{i\in N(\lambda)}\lambda_i f(\mathbf v_i)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The triangulation-induced affine interpolant is the convex envelope exactly when the stated inequality holds for every qualifying minimal affine dependency among the polytope vertices.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is a polytope with }V(X)=\{\mathbf v_1,\ldots,\mathbf v_k\}.
f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ admits a vertex polyhedral convex envelope over }X.
g_T(\mathbf x)=L_{f,\Delta}(\mathbf x)\text{ for }\mathbf x\in\Delta\in T.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_T=\operatorname{conv}_X f\iff\forall\lambda\text{ satisfying the stated minimal-affine-dependency conditions},\quad\sum_{i\in P(\lambda)}\lambda_i f(\mathbf v_i)\leq-\sum_{i\in N(\lambda)}\lambda_i f(\mathbf v_i).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex envelope of a concave function on a polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite vertex-mixture representation on a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\) be a polytope and let \(f:P\to\mathbb R\) be concave. For every \(x\in P\), the convex envelope \(\phi\) of \(f\) on \(P\) is
\[
\phi(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f(v_i):\lambda_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i v_i=x,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope of a concave function on a polytope is obtained by minimizing the convex combination of its vertex values over all vertex representations of the given point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i f(v_i):\lambda\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i v_i=x,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Polyhedral Convex Envelopes on Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between finite affine representability and vertex generation for continuously differentiable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(X\) is a polytope, then \(f\) has a polyhedral convex envelope over \(X\) if and only if \(G(f,X)=V(X)\), equivalently, if and only if \(f\) has a vertex polyhedral convex envelope over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable function on a polytope, the convex envelope is polyhedral exactly when its generating set is the vertex set of the polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ has a polyhedral convex envelope over }X\iff G(f,X)=V(X)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Concavity Excludes a Nonvertex Point from the Generating Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exclusion condition for generating points of a convex envelope on a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be lower semicontinuous and let \(X\) be a polytope. Let \(\bar x\in X\setminus V(X)\). If there is a line \(\ell\) such that \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}(\ell\cap X)\) and \(f\) is concave in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\) over \(\operatorname{ri}(\ell\cap X)\), then \(\bar x\notin G(f,X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower semicontinuous function on a polytope, a nonvertex point is excluded from the envelope generating set when it lies in the relative interior of a line section along which the function is locally concave near that point.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is concave in a neighborhood of }\bar x\text{ over }\operatorname{ri}(\ell\cap X)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\notin G(f,X)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additivity criterion for convex envelopes of edge-concave functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes convex-envelope additivity for two edge-concave functions on a polytope through vertex polyhedrality and intersections of linearity domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a polytope, and let \(f\) and \(g\) be edge-concave functions on \(P\). Let \(F_i\), \(i\in I\), be the linearity domains of \(f\), and let \(G_j\), \(j\in J\), be the linearity domains of \(g\). Then the following are equivalent: (i) \(\operatorname{conv}_{f,P}+\operatorname{conv}_{g,P}\) is vertex polyhedral; (ii) \(\operatorname{conv}_{f,P}+\operatorname{conv}_{g,P}=\operatorname{conv}_{f+g,P}\); and (iii) \(V(F_i\cap G_j)\subseteq V(P)\) for all \(i\in I\) and \(j\in J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two edge-concave functions on a polytope, the sum of their convex envelopes is vertex polyhedral if and only if it equals the convex envelope of their sum, which is also equivalent to every vertex of every intersection of their linearity domains being a vertex of the original polytope.
assumptions_latex: \{F_i:i\in I\}\text{ and }\{G_j:j\in J\}\text{ are the respective linearity domains of }f\text{ and }g
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\operatorname{conv}_{f,P}+\operatorname{conv}_{g,P}\text{ is vertex polyhedral}\right)\iff\left(\operatorname{conv}_{f,P}+\operatorname{conv}_{g,P}=\operatorname{conv}_{f+g,P}\right)\iff\left(\forall i\in I\,\forall j\in J,\ V(F_i\cap G_j)\subseteq V(P)\right).

children.title: Vertex–Facet Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dependence of envelope descriptions on vertex-based or facet-based domain data.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex–Facet Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How polytope representations determine concave-data envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^q\), and suppose \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}=\operatorname{conv}V\) is a nonempty compact polytope with vertex set \(V\). For every concave function \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\), the convex envelope depends on the domain through \(V\) and on \(f\) only through \(\{f(v):v\in V\}\):
\[(\operatorname{conv}_P f)(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v f(v):\lambda_v\ge0,\ \sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1,\ \sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv=x\right\}.\]
Consequently, if \(f,h:P\to\mathbb{R}\) are concave and satisfy \(f(v)=h(v)\) for every \(v\in V\), then \(\operatorname{conv}_P f=\operatorname{conv}_P h\). The halfspace system \(Ax\le b\) affects the formula through the polytope and its induced vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For concave functions on a compact polytope, the convex envelope is determined by the vertex values; the facet description matters through the polytope and the vertices it induces.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}=\operatorname{conv}V\) is a nonempty compact polytope with vertex set \(V\).
\(f,h:P\to\mathbb{R}\) are concave for the coincidence assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f(v)=h(v)\) for every \(v\in V\), then \(\operatorname{conv}_P f=\operatorname{conv}_P h\).

notation.meaning: Data of a halfspace representation of P.
Nonnegative mixture weight assigned to vertex v.
A second concave function on P used in the coincidence assertion.

children.title: General Convex-Domain Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope constructions beyond boxes and polytopes.

knowledge_statements.title: General Convex-Domain Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex envelopes on arbitrary finite-dimensional convex domains, without polyhedral structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) admit a convex minorant. The convex envelope of \(f\) relative to \(C\) is
\[(\operatorname{conv}_C f)(x)=\sup\{g(x):g\text{ is convex on }C,\ g(y)\le f(y)\text{ for every }y\in C\}.\]
It is equivalently the infimum of \(\sum_i\lambda_i f(x_i)\) over finite convex mixtures satisfying \(x_i\in C\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i x_i=x\). No vertex or facet representation of \(C\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On any convex domain, the envelope is the greatest convex minorant and can be computed conceptually through finite mixtures of domain points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}_C f=\sup\{g:g\text{ convex on }C,\ g\le f\}\).

children.title: Nonconvex-Domain Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Interaction between function envelopes and convexification of a nonconvex domain.

assumptions_latex: The extension \(g=f+\delta_D\) admits an affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g^{**}\) is the closed convex envelope generated by values of \(f\) on the original nonconvex domain, with effective domain contained in \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}D\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real function equal to f on D and positive infinity outside D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-envelope convention on the convexification of a nonconvex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \(g(x)=f(x)\) for \(x\in D\) and \(g(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. The closed convex envelope of \(f\) relative to \(D\) is \(g^{**}\). Its epigraph satisfies \[\operatorname{epi}g^{**}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}g),\] and \(g^{**}(x)=+\infty\) outside \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}D\). Thus convexifying the domain does not assign arbitrary data on new points: envelope values are determined by convex combinations and limits of epigraph points originating in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extend the function by positive infinity outside its nonconvex domain. Its biconjugate is the closed convex envelope on the convexified domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Domain Envelopes

children.title: Envelope Properness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings supporting proper convex envelopes or affine minorants.

children.title: Proper Envelope Regimes
children.top_down_role: Domain plus function settings supporting proper convex envelopes.

assumptions_latex: There exist \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(\langle a,x\rangle+b\le g(x)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed convex envelope \(g^{**}\) is proper and satisfies \(\langle a,x\rangle+b\le g^{**}(x)\le g(x)\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel biconjugate, interpreted as the closed convex envelope.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properness criterion for finite-dimensional extended-real closed convex envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper extended-real function \(g\) is in the proper-envelope regime precisely when it has a finite affine minorant. Under this condition, the Fenchel biconjugate \(g^{**}\) never takes the value \(-\infty\), is finite at some point of \(\operatorname{dom}g\), and is therefore proper. Moreover, \[\langle a,x\rangle+b\le g^{**}(x)\le g(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb{R}^n).\] Conversely, if \(g^{**}\) is proper, then its finite-dimensional closed convex epigraph admits a supporting affine minorant, which also minorizes \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper function has a proper closed convex envelope exactly when it possesses a finite affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.title: Proper Envelope Regimes

children.title: Affine-Minorant Existence
children.top_down_role: Settings supporting affine lower bounds for envelope construction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite affine minorant of \(g\) exists if and only if \(\operatorname{dom}g^*\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-domain test for existence of a global finite affine underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a finite affine function \(x\mapsto\langle a,x\rangle+b\) minorizes \(g\) exactly when \[b\le\inf_x\bigl(g(x)-\langle a,x\rangle\bigr)=-g^*(a).\] Consequently, some finite affine minorant exists if and only if \(g^*(a)<+\infty\) for at least one \(a\), equivalently \(\operatorname{dom}g^*\ne\varnothing\). For any such \(a\), the largest admissible intercept is \(-g^*(a)\), and every \(b\le-g^*(a)\) yields an affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine minorant exists exactly when the Fenchel conjugate is finite at some slope; its best intercept is minus the conjugate value.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Minorant Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conjugate-domain criterion is mathematically standard and precise, but “Part I Convex Analysis” is not a section, theorem, definition, or page-level locator as required.

children.title: Improperness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where proper envelope objects or affine minorants cease to be available.

knowledge_statements.title: Improperness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete coercivity-at-minus-infinity boundary showing loss of envelope properness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be given by \(g(x)=-x^2\). There is no finite affine function \(x\mapsto ax+b\) satisfying \(ax+b\le g(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). Under the convention that extended-real convex underestimators may take the value \(-\infty\), the convex envelope is \[\operatorname{conv}g(x)=-\infty\qquad(x\in\mathbb{R}).\] Thus a finite-valued function need not have a proper convex envelope when it lacks a global affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite function minus x squared has no affine lower bound, so its extended-real convex envelope is minus infinity everywhere.
assumptions_latex: Extended-real convex underestimators are allowed to take \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(g(x)=-x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), the convex envelope is identically \(-\infty\) and hence improper.

notation.meaning: Greatest extended-real convex function bounded above by g.

children.title: Envelope Attainment
children.top_down_role: Attainment and nonattainment in geometric and mixture representations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixture formula for the convex envelope attains its minimum using at most \(n+1\) points of \(D\).

notation.meaning: Convex envelope of f relative to D.
Simplex of nonnegative weights summing to one.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact finite-dimensional mixture attainment with a Carathéodory support bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}D\), the convex envelope value is attained in the finite-mixture representation \[f_D^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i f(x_i):1\le m\le n+1,\ x_i\in D,\ \lambda\in\Delta_m,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i x_i=x\right\}.\] Compactness of \(D\) and continuity of \(f\) ensure attainment, while the support may be chosen with at most \(n+1\) points. Without compactness or suitable level compactness, the corresponding infimum can be finite but unattained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain with continuous data, every convex-envelope value is realized by a mixture of at most n plus one domain points.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Attainment

children.title: Relaxation–Envelope Coincidence
children.top_down_role: Problem classes in which a tractable relaxation recovers the envelope.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation–Envelope Coincidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraphical exactness criterion for a closed convex lifted relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(r_R(x)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb{R}:(x,t)\in R\}\), taking \(r_R(x)=+\infty\) when the section is empty. Suppose every nonempty vertical section of \(R\) is bounded below. Then \(R=\operatorname{epi}r_R\), and the relaxation recovers the closed convex envelope exactly when \[R=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}g)=\operatorname{epi}g^{**}.\] Equivalently, \(r_R(x)=g^{**}(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The inclusion \(\operatorname{epi}g^{**}\subseteq R\) implies \(r_R\le g^{**}\); if the inclusion is strict, the inequality is strict at some point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex upward-closed relaxation with no downward-unbounded vertical section recovers the envelope exactly when it is the closed convex hull of the original epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and has an affine minorant.
\(R\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) is closed, convex, and upward closed in its last coordinate.
Every nonempty vertical section \(\{t\in\mathbb{R}:(x,t)\in R\}\) is bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation value function equals \(g^{**}\) exactly when \(R=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{epi}g)\).

notation.meaning: Lower-bound function induced by the lifted relaxation R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Moment and Polynomial Formulations of a Rational Convex Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment, zero duality gap, and exact convex-envelope recovery by the formulations defined in (11.5) and (11.7).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p,q\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\), with \(q>0\) on \(\mathbb K\), let \(f\) be as in (11.4), and set \(\mathbf D=\operatorname{co}(\mathbb K)\). For every \(\mathbf x\in\mathbf D\), the problems (11.5) and (11.7) have optimal solutions, there is no duality gap, and
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{pop}}(\mathbf x)=\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}(\mathbf x)=\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}^{1}(\mathbf x)=\widehat f(\mathbf x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified rational-function setting, the moment and polynomial formulations attain optimal solutions at every point of the convex hull, have equal optimal values, and recover the convex envelope exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Problems (11.5) and (11.7) attain optimal solutions and }\rho_{\mathrm{pop}}(\mathbf x)=\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}(\mathbf x)=\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}^{1}(\mathbf x)=\widehat f(\mathbf x)\quad\forall\mathbf x\in\mathbf D

children.top_down_role: Upper approximation partners required for equality, range, and two-sided constraint relaxation.

children.title: Concave-Envelope Representations
children.top_down_role: Upper-envelope counterparts of geometric and variational convex-envelope constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The concave envelope satisfies \(f_D^{\mathrm{ccv}}=-(-f)_D^{\mathrm{cv}}\) and has an attained maximum-mixture representation.

notation.meaning: Least concave majorant of f on the convex hull of D.
Greatest convex minorant relative to D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional upper-envelope representation dual to the convex-envelope mixture formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The concave envelope of \(f\) relative to \(D\) is obtained by sign reversal: \[f_D^{\mathrm{ccv}}(x)=-(-f)_D^{\mathrm{cv}}(x).\] Equivalently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}D\), \[f_D^{\mathrm{ccv}}(x)=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i f(x_i):1\le m\le n+1,\ x_i\in D,\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i x_i=x\right\}.\] It is the pointwise least concave function majorizing \(f\) on \(D\), and compactness with continuity ensures that the displayed maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The concave envelope is the negative convex envelope of the negated function and equals the largest feasible mixture value.
knowledge_statements.title: Concave-Envelope Representations

children.title: Paired Convex–Concave Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Coupled lower and upper approximations for shared nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid paired relaxation satisfies \(\ell(x)\le f(x)\le u(x)\) on \(C\), with \(\ell\) convex and \(u\) concave.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise paired relaxation for one nonlinear expression over a shared convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A paired convex–concave relaxation of \(f\) on \(C\) is a pair \((\ell,u)\) such that \(\ell:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex, \(u:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) is concave, and \[\ell(x)\le f(x)\le u(x)\qquad(x\in C).\] The pair is envelope-exact when \(\ell\) is the convex envelope of \(f\) and \(u\) is its concave envelope on \(C\). For a shared auxiliary variable \(w\) representing \(f(x)\), the inequalities \(\ell(x)\le w\le u(x)\) give the associated two-sided relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A paired relaxation places a convex lower bound and concave upper bound around the same nonlinear expression on one domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Paired Convex–Concave Relaxations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex–concave relaxation of a univariate composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule combining convex and concave bounds on an inner function with the corresponding envelopes of an outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let p be a convex minorant and q a concave majorant of t on S. Let \varphi and \Phi be the convex and concave envelopes, respectively, of F on [a,b]. Suppose t_{\min},t_{\max}\in[a,b] satisfy
\[
F(t_{\min})=\inf_{a\le z\le b}F(z),\qquad F(t_{\max})=\sup_{a\le z\le b}F(z).
\]
Then, on X=\{x\in S:a\le t(x)\le b\},
\[
\varphi\!\left(\operatorname{mid}[p(x),q(x),t_{\min}]\right)
\]
is a convex minorant of F(t(x)), and
\[
\Phi\!\left(\operatorname{mid}[p(x),q(x),t_{\max}]\right)
\]
is a concave majorant of F(t(x)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the middle of the inner function's lower bound, upper bound, and an extremizer of the outer function, then applying the appropriate outer envelope, produces convex and concave relaxations of the composition.
assumptions_latex: p\text{ is convex on }S\text{ and }p(x)\le t(x)\text{ on }S
q\text{ is concave on }S\text{ and }t(x)\le q(x)\text{ on }S
t_{\min},t_{\max}\in[a,b]\text{ attain the minimum and maximum of }F\text{ on }[a,b]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi(\operatorname{mid}[p,q,t_{\min}])\le F\circ t\le\Phi(\operatorname{mid}[p,q,t_{\max}])\quad\text{on }X.

children.title: Two-Sided Relaxation Quality
children.top_down_role: Ordering and tightening of paired lower and upper approximation objects.

assumptions_latex: \((\ell_1,u_1)\) and \((\ell_2,u_2)\) are valid paired relaxations of \(f\) on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second pair is at least as tight, and \(0\le u_2-\ell_2\le u_1-\ell_1\) pointwise.

notation.meaning: Pointwise relaxation width of a paired approximation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance order and width measure for two-sided relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((\ell_2,u_2)\) is tighter than \((\ell_1,u_1)\) when \[\ell_1(x)\le\ell_2(x)\le f(x)\le u_2(x)\le u_1(x)\qquad(x\in C).\] This order implies the pointwise width inequality \[0\le u_2(x)-\ell_2(x)\le u_1(x)-\ell_1(x).\] Equality \(u_i(x)=\ell_i(x)\) certifies exact recovery of \(f(x)\) at that point. Among all valid pairs, the convex and concave envelopes form the tightest pair: every convex lower approximation lies below the convex envelope, and every concave upper approximation lies above the concave envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raising the lower bound and lowering the upper bound tightens a paired relaxation and cannot increase its pointwise width.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Relaxation Quality

children.title: Univariate Envelopes

children.title: Single-Curvature Primitives
children.top_down_role: Convex or concave primitives governed by tangent and secant geometry.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For one curvature sign, one envelope is \(f\) and the opposite envelope is the endpoint secant.

notation.meaning: Affine secant interpolating the endpoint values of f.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interval envelopes for globally convex or globally concave scalar primitives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_f\) be the endpoint secant \[s_f(x)=\frac{b-x}{b-a}f(a)+\frac{x-a}{b-a}f(b).\] If \(f\) is convex on \([a,b]\), then its convex envelope is \(f\) itself and its concave envelope is \(s_f\). If \(f\) is concave, the roles reverse: its convex envelope is \(s_f\) and its concave envelope is \(f\). When \(f\) is differentiable and convex, each tangent \(x\mapsto f(t)+f'(t)(x-t)\) is a valid convex underestimator; for differentiable concave \(f\), each tangent is a valid concave overestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an interval, a single-curvature function is one exact envelope, while its endpoint secant is the opposite envelope.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Curvature Primitives

children.title: Mixed-Curvature Primitives
children.top_down_role: Single- and multiple-inflection primitives requiring piecewise envelope geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Curvature Primitives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-inflection concave-then-convex primitive; other curvature orders require the corresponding reflected or sign-reversed formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(L_{a,t}(x)=f(a)+\frac{f(t)-f(a)}{t-a}(x-a)\). Under the stated one-inflection hypotheses, the convex envelope of \(f\) on \([a,b]\) is \[f^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)=\begin{cases}L_{a,t}(x),&a\le x\le t,\\ f(x),&t\le x\le b.\end{cases}\] When \(t<b\), the contact condition is \[f'(t)=\frac{f(t)-f(a)}{t-a}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated concave-then-convex geometry and chord-validity condition, the convex envelope is the chord from the left endpoint to the contact point, followed by the original convex branch.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1([a,b])\) is concave on \([a,c]\) and convex on \([c,b]\).
There is \(t\in(c,b]\) such that \(L_{a,t}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in[a,t]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chord-to-contact followed by \(f\) is the convex envelope under the stated one-inflection geometry.

notation.meaning: Chord joining the graph points at a and t.

children.title: Nonsmooth Univariate Primitives
children.top_down_role: Absolute-value and related nonsmooth scalar primitives.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex envelope is \(|x|\), while the concave envelope is its endpoint secant.

notation.meaning: Endpoint secant of the absolute-value function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical absolute-value primitive, including intervals that cross its nondifferentiable point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(x\mapsto|x|\) is convex on every interval, its convex envelope on \([a,b]\) is \[f^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)=|x|.\] Its concave envelope is the endpoint secant \[f^{\mathrm{ccv}}(x)=\frac{b-x}{b-a}|a|+\frac{x-a}{b-a}|b|.\] If \(0\notin(a,b)\), the absolute-value function is affine on the interval and both envelopes coincide with \(f\). If \(a<0<b\), the convex envelope retains the kink at zero, whereas the concave envelope is the single affine chord joining \((a,|a|)\) and \((b,|b|)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute value is its own convex envelope; its concave envelope is the endpoint chord, coinciding with it when the interval does not cross zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Univariate Primitives
