children.title: Singular Primitives
children.top_down_role: Reciprocal, logarithmic, root, plus related primitives with singular behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Primitives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local definition for univariate primitives singular at a finite domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subsetneq\mathbb R\) be an interval and let \(\phi:D\to\mathbb R\) be continuous on \(\operatorname{int}D\). The primitive \(\phi\) is singular at a finite boundary point \(a\in\partial D\) if it is not Lipschitz on any one-sided neighborhood of \(a\) in \(D\); equivalently for differentiable \(\phi\), it suffices that \(\lvert\phi'(t)\rvert\) be unbounded as \(t\to a\) within \(D\). It is a singular primitive if it is singular at at least one finite boundary point of its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular primitive loses local Lipschitz regularity at a finite domain boundary, typically through an unbounded one-sided derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subsetneq\mathbb R\) is an interval with a finite boundary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\) is singular when it fails one-sided local Lipschitz continuity at some finite \(a\in\partial D\).

notation.meaning: finite boundary point of the domain

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed meaning of “singular primitive” is not standard enough to adopt without a source. The derivative characterization also requires differentiability throughout the relevant one-sided neighborhood and should distinguish unboundedness from divergence.

children.title: Restricted-Domain Primitives
children.top_down_role: Primitive envelopes whose validity depends on qualified input domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Domain Primitives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real encoding of a primitive whose formula is valid only on a prescribed interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R\) be an interval and let \(\phi:D\to\mathbb R\). Its restricted-domain extension is the function \(\bar\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) defined by \[\bar\phi(t)=\begin{cases}\phi(t),&t\in D,\\+\infty,&t\notin D.\end{cases}\] Thus any optimization model containing \(\bar\phi(t)\) implicitly enforces \(t\in D\). If \(D\) is convex and \(\phi\) is convex on \(D\), then \(\bar\phi\) is an extended-real convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-domain primitive equals its formula on an interval and positive infinity outside, thereby encoding domain feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}\bar\phi=D\), and convexity of \(\phi\) on \(D\) implies convexity of \(\bar\phi\).

children.title: Domain-Boundary Singularities
children.top_down_role: Envelope behavior near excluded points or singular domain boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Boundary Singularities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary exclusion required when a primitive or its derivatives diverge at the domain endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R\), let \(a\in\partial D\) be finite, and let \(\phi\) be finite on \(\operatorname{int}D\). If \(\lvert\phi(t)\rvert\to+\infty\) or \(\lvert\phi'(t)\rvert\to+\infty\) as \(t\to a\) within \(D\), then any relaxation using finite function values or a finite tangent slope at \(a\) is invalid. Tangent-based underestimators must instead be generated at points in \(\operatorname{int}D\); if \(\phi(t)\to+\infty\), the singular endpoint cannot belong to the finite-valued feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divergent boundary values or slopes invalidate finite tangents at the endpoint; cuts must use interior points and respect the effective domain.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) is a finite boundary point of \(D\).
\(\phi\) is differentiable on the relevant side of \(\operatorname{int}D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite tangent construction at \(a\) is valid when \(\phi(a)\) or the required one-sided derivative is nonfinite.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The endpoint warning fits the failure-boundary container, but the assertion that any relaxation using a finite endpoint value or slope is invalid depends on the precise tangent construction and extended-domain convention. No source supports those details.

children.title: Bilinear Box Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Hull-strength convex and concave relaxations for bounded bilinear terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Box Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCormick convex-hull representation for one bounded bilinear graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\), \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), and \(w=xy\), with finite bounds. The convex hull of the graph is described by \[w\ge \ell_x y+\ell_y x-\ell_x\ell_y,\qquad w\ge u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y,\] \[w\le u_x y+\ell_y x-u_x\ell_y,\qquad w\le \ell_x y+u_y x-\ell_xu_y.\] Consequently, the convex envelope of \(xy\) is the maximum of the two lower affine functions, and its concave envelope is the minimum of the two upper affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four McCormick inequalities give the exact convex hull of a bounded bilinear graph and its convex and concave envelopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed polytope equals \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,w):w=xy\}\) over the box.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex envelope of a bilinear term on a box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-affine McCormick lower envelope on a nondegenerate rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^L<x^U\) and \(y^L<y^U\). On \([x^L,x^U]\times[y^L,y^U]\), the convex envelope of \(xy\) is
\[
\phi(x,y)=\max\{x^Ly+y^Lx-x^Ly^L,\ x^Uy+y^Ux-x^Uy^U\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\phi(x,y)=\begin{cases}
x^Ly+y^Lx-x^Ly^L,&y\le-\dfrac{y^U-y^L}{x^U-x^L}x+\dfrac{x^Uy^U-x^Ly^L}{x^U-x^L},\\
x^Uy+y^Ux-x^Uy^U,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nondegenerate rectangle, the convex envelope of the bilinear term xy is the maximum of its two affine McCormick underestimators, with the stated line separating their active regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(x,y)=\max\{x^Ly+y^Lx-x^Ly^L,\ x^Uy+y^Ux-x^Uy^U\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum bilinear-envelope separation on a rectangle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case vertical gap between a bounded bilinear term and its convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^L\le x^U\), \(y^L\le y^U\), and
\[
\phi(x,y)=\max\{x^Ly+y^Lx-x^Ly^L,\ x^Uy+y^Ux-x^Uy^U\}.
\]
Then
\[
\max_{(x,y)\in[x^L,x^U]\times[y^L,y^U]}\bigl(xy-\phi(x,y)\bigr)=\frac{(x^U-x^L)(y^U-y^L)}4,
\]
and this value is attained at
\[
\left(\frac{x^L+x^U}{2},\frac{y^L+y^U}{2}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest vertical gap between xy and its convex envelope over a rectangle is one quarter of the rectangle's area and is attained at its midpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{(x,y)\in[x^L,x^U]\times[y^L,y^U]}(xy-\phi(x,y))=\frac{(x^U-x^L)(y^U-y^L)}4\text{, attained at }\left(\frac{x^L+x^U}{2},\frac{y^L+y^U}{2}\right)

children.title: Multilinear Hull Representations
children.top_down_role: Vertex, facet, and extended representations for multilinear terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Multilinear Hull Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact vertex-based extended formulation for a multilinear monomial over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), let \(V=\prod_{i=1}^n\{\ell_i,u_i\}\), and define \(m(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\). The graph hull has the extended representation \[x=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v v,\qquad w=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v m(v),\qquad \sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1,\qquad \lambda_v\ge0.\] Its projection onto \((x,w)\) equals \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,m(x)):x\in B\}\). Eliminating the multipliers yields an equivalent, potentially large, facet representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilinear graph hull is the convex combination of its box-vertex graph points; projecting the vertex formulation gives the exact hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of the displayed simplex formulation is the exact multilinear graph hull.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The vertex formulation is mathematically standard, but the cited generic convex-hull section does not specifically support the crucial claim that a multilinear graph over a box is generated by its vertex graph points. A multilinear-specific locator is required.

children.title: Recursive Bilinearization
children.top_down_role: Alternative product groupings and their formulation-dependent strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Bilinearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-structured reduction of a multilinear product to bounded bilinear factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite bounds for \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) and a binary tree whose leaves are these variables. For each internal node with child values \(p\) and \(q\), introduce \(z=pq\), propagate a valid finite interval for \(z\), and replace \(z=pq\) by its four bilinear box-envelope inequalities. Process nodes from leaves to root and output the root variable as the surrogate for \(\prod_{i=1}^n x_i\). The result is a convex relaxation; different trees can produce different projected relaxations and need not yield the multilinear graph hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively group factors, introduce one variable per partial product, and impose McCormick inequalities; different grouping trees can have different strength.
assumptions_latex: All leaf and propagated product bounds are finite.
A binary factorization tree is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed formulation contains every exact product point but may strictly contain the multilinear graph hull.

source_refs.locator: Part I. Biconvex and Bilinear Problems

source_witnesses.locator: Part I. Biconvex and Bilinear Problems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its non-hull caveat fit the container, but “Part I” is not a sufficiently specific locator and does not inspectably support the claims about tree-dependent projected strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Product Disaggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening obtained by partitioning product domains before convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a bounded box and let \(\mathcal P=\{B_k\}_{k=1}^K\) be a finite box partition of \(B\). For each cell, construct a valid product relaxation \(R_k\), such as the bilinear box hull, and form a valid disjunctive extended formulation for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K R_k)\). Its projection is a valid relaxation of the product graph on \(B\). If \(\mathcal P'\) refines \(\mathcal P\) and the same cellwise envelope construction is used, then the refined projected relaxation is contained in the coarse one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning the product domain and convexifying each cell yields a valid relaxation; nested refinement cannot weaken the projected relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is bounded and \(\mathcal P\) is a finite box partition.
Each \(R_k\) validly relaxes the product graph on \(B_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a refinement \(\mathcal P'\), the relaxations satisfy \(R(\mathcal P')\subseteq R(\mathcal P)\).

notation.meaning: finite partition of the product domain

children.title: Separable Quadratic Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise convexification of separable quadratic terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Quadratic Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise convex envelope of a separable quadratic over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\), let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) have finite bounds, and let \(f:B\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(f(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n(a_i x_i^2+b_i x_i)\). Its convex envelope is separable: \[\operatorname{vex}_B f(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(b_i x_i+g_i(x_i)\bigr),\] where \(g_i(t)=a_i t^2\) if \(a_i\ge0\), while, if \(a_i<0\), \[g_i(t)=a_i(\ell_i+u_i)t-a_i\ell_i u_i.\] The latter expression is the chord joining the endpoint values of the concave quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive integer dimension and a finite box, the convex envelope of a separable quadratic is the sum of its coordinate envelopes: convex terms remain unchanged and concave terms become endpoint chords.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is separable and has no cross-products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_B f\) equals the displayed sum of exact univariate envelopes.

children.title: Spectral-Diagonal Curvature Corrections
children.top_down_role: Curvature modification based on eigenstructure and diagonal perturbations.

children.title: Spectral Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Curvature modification organized through eigenstructure.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar eigenvalue correction for an indefinite quadratic on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\), let \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) have finite bounds. Choose \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\) and define \[q_\alpha(x)=q(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i).\] Since each added factor is nonpositive on \(B\), \(q_\alpha(x)\le q(x)\) on \(B\). Moreover, \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\), so \(q_\alpha\) is convex and is a spectral underestimator of \(q\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional quadratic on a finite box, a scalar diagonal shift at least as large as the negative minimum eigenvalue produces a convex quadratic lying below the original throughout the box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_\alpha\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) and satisfies \(q_\alpha(x)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).

children.title: Diagonal Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Curvature modification using coordinatewise diagonal perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-specific diagonal curvature correction for an indefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\), let \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) have finite bounds. For any \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfying \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\), define \[q_\alpha(x)=q(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i).\] Then \(q_\alpha\) is convex, and because every correction term is nonpositive on its interval, \(q_\alpha(x)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional quadratic on a finite box, nonnegative coordinatewise diagonal shifts that make the quadratic matrix positive semidefinite produce convex box-valid underestimators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_\alpha\) is a convex underestimator of \(q\) on \(B\).

children.title: Spectral–Diagonal Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Strength, scaling, plus structural differences between the two correction families.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral–Diagonal Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family inclusion and the limits of pointwise comparison between scalar and diagonal corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric quadratic matrix \(Q\), every feasible spectral correction \(\bar\alpha I\), with \(\bar\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\), is feasible for the diagonal family by choosing \(\alpha_i=\bar\alpha\) for all \(i\). Hence optimizing any common underestimator-quality criterion over feasible diagonal corrections cannot be worse than optimizing it over scalar spectral corrections. However, two distinct feasible corrections need not be pointwise ordered on the box because the quantities \((x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i)\) vary by coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar spectral shifts form a subset of diagonal shifts, so optimized diagonal corrections are no worse under a shared criterion, although arbitrary choices need not dominate pointwise.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) and all box bounds are finite.
Both families use the same box-correction formula and quality criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral family is contained in the diagonal family, but arbitrary feasible members have no universal pointwise ordering.

children.title: Lifted Quadratic Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Matrix and product-variable liftings for quadratic lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Quadratic Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex matrix lifting that replaces quadratic products by linear lifted variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), so that \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\). Replace the rank-one equality by a convex set containing it, for example \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\] together with valid box product inequalities for \(X_{ij}=x_ix_j\). Minimizing \(\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) over this lifted feasible set gives a lower bound on the original box-constrained quadratic problem because every point \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift products into a matrix, relax rank one by semidefinite and box-product constraints, and minimize the resulting linear objective for a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: All added lifted constraints are valid for \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted optimum is no greater than the original minimization optimum.

notation.meaning: matrix inner product replacing the quadratic form

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nontriviality and positivity properties of \(W\)

children.title: Quadratic-Constraint Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification families for nonconvex quadratic constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Constraint Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal quadratic correction on a bounded box; the resulting inequality is a valid convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\) on \(B=[\ell,u]\), and define
\[
q_d(x)=q(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n d_i(x_i-\ell_i)(x_i-u_i).
\]
If \(d\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(d)\succeq0\), then \(q_d\) is convex and \(q_d(x)\le q(x)\) for every \(x\in B\). In particular,
\[
\{x\in B:q(x)\le0\}\subseteq\{x\in B:q_d(x)\le0\},
\]
so \(q_d(x)\le0\) is a valid convex relaxation of \(q(x)\le0\) over \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative diagonal box correction that makes the quadratic curvature positive semidefinite produces a convex lower bound and a valid relaxation of the quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_d\) is a convex underestimator of \(q\) on \(B\), and \(q(x)\le0\Rightarrow q_d(x)\le0\).

children.title: Scaling-Sensitive Envelope Family
children.top_down_role: Primitive families whose convexification depends on signs, exponents, scaling, and denominator domains.

children.title: Power-Monomial Envelope Family
children.top_down_role: Signed-power and multivariate-monomial convexification regimes.

children.title: Power Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Convexification regimes for univariate power primitives.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_{[\ell,u]}x^p=x^p\) and \(\operatorname{cav}_{[\ell,u]}x^p=L_p(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact univariate envelopes for a nonnegative power with exponent at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f_p(x)=x^p\) on \([\ell,u]\subset[0,\infty)\) with \(p\ge1\), the function \(f_p\) is convex. Its convex envelope is therefore itself. Its concave envelope is the endpoint secant
\[
L_p(x)=\frac{u-x}{u-\ell}\ell^p+\frac{x-\ell}{u-\ell}u^p.
\]
Thus, for every \(x\in[\ell,u]\),
\[
\operatorname{vex}_{[\ell,u]}f_p(x)=x^p\le L_p(x)=\operatorname{cav}_{[\ell,u]}f_p(x).
\]
For \(0<p<1\), the two roles reverse because the power is concave on the nonnegative interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonnegative interval, a power with exponent at least one is its own convex envelope, while its endpoint secant is the concave envelope.
knowledge_statements.title: Power Envelopes

children.title: Multivariate Monomial Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Convexification regimes for products of powered variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Monomial Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General convex-closure representation; specialized sign and exponent regimes may yield simpler formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\in\mathbb R^n\) and let \(m(x)=\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{\alpha_j}\) be finite and continuous on a nonempty compact convex set \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\). For every \(x\in B\),
\[
m_B^{\mathrm{vex}}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_k m(x^k):N\in\mathbb N,\ \lambda_k\ge0,\ \sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_k=1,\ x^k\in B,\ \sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_kx^k=x\right\}.
\]
This function is the greatest convex function dominated by \(m\) on \(B\). The analogous supremum over the same barycentric representations is the concave envelope. The domain \(B\) must contain only points at which the selected real power branches are defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multivariate monomial's convex envelope is the infimum of convex combinations of its values at domain points whose barycenter is the evaluation point.
assumptions_latex: \(m(x)=\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{\alpha_j}\) is finite and continuous on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m^{\mathrm{vex}}_B(x)\) equals the infimum of convex combinations of monomial values whose base points average to \(x\).

children.title: Sign–Exponent Regimes
children.top_down_role: Envelope changes induced by variable signs plus exponent patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign–Exponent Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-valuedness and curvature regimes governing which power-envelope formula is admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R\), the real power function \(f_p(x)=x^p\) on \((0,\infty)\) is convex when \(p\le0\) or \(p\ge1\), and concave when \(0\le p\le1\). It is constant at \(p=0\) and affine at \(p=1\). A finite continuous extension to \(x=0\) exists for \(p>0\), apart from separately specified conventions at \(p=0\). On negative arguments, real-valuedness requires an admissible exponent branch, such as an integer exponent or a reduced rational exponent with odd denominator. An envelope on an interval meeting nonpositive values therefore requires an explicit sign and exponent regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power curvature changes at exponents zero and one, while intervals containing nonpositive values require explicit real-branch and finiteness conditions.
assumptions_latex: Powers on \((0,\infty)\) use the standard real branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^p\) is convex for \(p\le0\) or \(p\ge1\), and concave for \(0\le p\le1\), on \((0,\infty)\).

notation.meaning: Real power function on the positive half-line.

children.title: Fractional Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Ratio convexification under sign-stable denominator regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linear-fractional function is both quasiconvex and quasiconcave, and the stated scaling gives an exact lifted representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-fractional structure under a strictly positive denominator; sign stability is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
r(x)=\frac{a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta}{c^{\mathsf T}x+\delta},
\]
with positive denominator on \(C\), every sublevel set satisfies
\[
\{x\in C:r(x)\le\gamma\}=\{x\in C:(a-\gamma c)^{\mathsf T}x+\beta-\gamma\delta\le0\},
\]
and every superlevel set has the reversed affine inequality. Thus \(r\) is both quasiconvex and quasiconcave. The substitution \(s=(c^{\mathsf T}x+\delta)^{-1}\), \(y=sx\) gives the exact lifted relations
\[
c^{\mathsf T}y+\delta s=1,\qquad y\in sC,\qquad r(x)=a^{\mathsf T}y+\beta s,\qquad s>0.
\]
These relations fail without a denominator of fixed nonzero sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-denominator linear fraction has affine level sets and an exact scaled lifting; crossing a zero denominator invalidates this representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record establishes quasiconvexity and a Charnes–Cooper-type lifting for a linear-fractional function, but it gives no convex or concave envelope or underestimator. It therefore does not fit the Fractional Envelopes terminal container.

children.title: Perspective Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Perspective-based convexification of scaled and on–off convex structure.

assumptions_latex: \(t>0\), with the closed extension used at \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed perspective \(\widetilde f\) is convex and its epigraph is the closed conic hull of \(\{(x,1,r):r\ge f(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Recession function of the closed convex function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective representation, including its recession-value convention at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed perspective of \(f\) is
\[
\widetilde f(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
t f(x/t),&t>0,\\
f^{\infty}(x),&t=0,\\
+\infty,&t<0.
\end{cases}
\]
It is a closed convex function, and
\[
\operatorname{epi}\widetilde f=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(x,1,r):r\ge f(x)\}.
\]
Consequently, an inequality \(r\ge t f(x/t)\) with \(t>0\) is convex in \((x,t,r)\). The closed value at \(t=0\) is required for exact hull descriptions and prevents loss of recession points when the scaling variable can vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling a closed convex function by its positive perspective preserves convexity; the recession extension at zero scale yields the closed conic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Envelopes

children.title: Selection-Controlled Primitive Family
children.top_down_role: Convexification of selectors, extrema, piecewise functions, and indicator-controlled nonlinear expressions.

children.title: Finite-Extremum Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Relaxation families for finite extrema of nonlinear expressions.

children.title: Minimum Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Lower-model families for finite minima of nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex envelope of a finite pointwise minimum via its disjunctive epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(h(x)=\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\) on \(C\). Its restricted epigraph satisfies
\[
\operatorname{epi}_C h=\bigcup_{i=1}^m\{(x,t):x\in C,\ t\ge f_i(x)\}.
\]
For every \(x\in C\), its convex envelope is
\[
h_C^{\mathrm{vex}}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_k f_{i_k}(x^k):N\in\mathbb N,\ \lambda_k\ge0,\ \sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_k=1,\ x^k\in C,\ i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\ \sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_kx^k=x\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, the epigraph of \(h_C^{\mathrm{vex}}\) is the closed convex hull of the union of the individual restricted epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex envelope of a finite pointwise minimum is obtained by convexifying the union of the pieces' restricted epigraphs, equivalently by barycentric mixing across pieces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed barycentric infimum is the convex envelope of \(h(x)=\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\) on \(C\).

notation.meaning: Convex envelope of the minimum on the domain.

children.title: Maximum Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Lower-model families for finite maxima of nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of convex underestimators under finite pointwise maxima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) and \(h(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\) on \(C\). If every \(\ell_i:C\to\mathbb R\) is convex and satisfies \(\ell_i(x)\le f_i(x)\) for all \(x\in C\), then
\[
\ell(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\ell_i(x)
\]
is convex and satisfies
\[
\ell(x)\le h(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
If every \(f_i\) is convex and \(\ell_i=f_i\), then \(h\) is convex and equals its convex envelope on \(C\). For general component underestimators, \(\ell\) need not equal the convex envelope of \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite maximum of convex componentwise lower bounds is a convex lower bound for the maximum. It is exact when the chosen component bounds equal convex original pieces, but not in general.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(\ell_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and satisfies \(\ell_i(x)\le f_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\ell_i(x)\) is convex and satisfies \(\ell(x)\le\max_{1\le i\le m} f_i(x)\) on \(C\).

notation.meaning: Pointwise maximum of the original functions.

children.title: Extremum Coupling Effects
children.top_down_role: Strength effects caused by shared variables across extremum branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Extremum Coupling Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of commuting componentwise convexification with a finite minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(C=[-1,1]\), let \(f_1(x)=x\) and \(f_2(x)=-x\). Both functions are affine and satisfy \(\operatorname{vex}_C f_i=f_i\). Their pointwise minimum is
\[
h(x)=\min\{x,-x\}=-|x|,
\]
whereas its convex envelope is
\[
\operatorname{vex}_C h(x)=-1\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{vex}_C\bigl(\min\{f_1,f_2\}\bigr)=-1\neq-|x|=\min\{\operatorname{vex}_C f_1,\operatorname{vex}_C f_2\}.
\]
Thus convex-envelope construction does not generally commute with a finite pointwise minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexification does not commute with a finite minimum: the minimum of two affine functions on this interval has a convex envelope strictly below their pointwise minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_C(\min\{f_1,f_2\})=-1\neq-|x|=\min\{\operatorname{vex}_Cf_1,\operatorname{vex}_Cf_2\}\).

notation.meaning: Pointwise minimum of the two affine pieces.

children.title: Piecewise-Defined Function Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Convexification across region-dependent function pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Defined Function Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact disjunctive convex envelope for finitely many compact convex regions and convex pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), and \(f(x)=f_i(x)\) for \(x\in C_i\), with the pieces agreeing on overlaps. For every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}C\), the convex closure generated by the piecewise function is
\[
f_C^{\mathrm{vex}}(x)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^{\pi}(z_i,\lambda_i):\sum_{i=1}^m z_i=x,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ z_i\in\lambda_i C_i\right\},
\]
where \(f_i^{\pi}(z,\lambda)=\lambda f_i(z/\lambda)\) for \(\lambda>0\), with the closed perspective value at \(\lambda=0\). Its epigraph is
\[
\operatorname{epi}f_C^{\mathrm{vex}}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m\operatorname{epi}_{C_i}f_i\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite piecewise convex function is convexified on the convex hull of its regions by mixing the regional epigraphs with perspective-scaled variables and weights.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
The piecewise function is single-valued wherever regions overlap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perspective-mixing formula gives the convex closure of the piecewise-defined function on \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i)\).

children.title: Indicator-Controlled Convexification
children.top_down_role: Hull-strength relaxations for nonlinear expressions controlled by discrete indicators.

children.title: Indicator Convexification
children.top_down_role: Hull-strength relaxations centered on discrete indicator controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex hull of a two-branch compact convex indicator disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
D=(S_0\times\{0\})\cup(S_1\times\{1\}),
\]
the convex hull is
\[
\operatorname{conv}D=\left\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ x=x^0+x^1,\ x^0\in(1-z)S_0,\ x^1\in zS_1\right\},
\]
with \(0S_i=\{0\}\). Thus the relaxation \(0\le z\le1\), together with disaggregated variables in the scaled branch sets, gives the exact continuous convex hull of the two indicator states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregating a two-state indicator into scaled copies of its branch sets gives the exact continuous convex hull of the binary disjunction.
assumptions_latex: The binary indicator \(z\) selects \(S_0\) when \(z=0\) and \(S_1\) when \(z=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed scaled-set formulation is exactly \(\operatorname{conv}((S_0\times\{0\})\cup(S_1\times\{1\}))\).

children.title: On–Off Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification of nonlinear expressions activated or deactivated by discrete states.

knowledge_statements.title: On–Off Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective hull for a convex epigraph activated by a binary on–off variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
S=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):x\in C,\ t\ge f(x)\}.
\]
Its closed convex hull is
\[
\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ x\in zC,\ t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z)\},
\]
where \(f^{\pi}(x,z)=z f(x/z)\) for \(z>0\), with the closed perspective value at \(z=0\). Since \(C\) is bounded and contains \(0\), the constraint \(x\in zC\) imposes \(x=0\) at \(z=0\). This formulation is the exact continuous hull of the stated on–off epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded convex on–off domain, the closed perspective of the active cost gives the exact hull and the scaled-domain constraint forces zero activity when the indicator vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, convex, and contains \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perspective inequality \(t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z)\), together with \(x\in zC\), describes the closed convex hull of the on–off epigraph.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the active cost.

children.title: Hull-Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Domain plus formulation settings governing hull-level relaxation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Hull-Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares closed continuous relaxations of an indicator-controlled convex feasible set by set inclusion and ideality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and define \(S=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\{0,1\}: z=0\Rightarrow x=0,\ z=1\Rightarrow x\in C\}\). A closed convex relaxation \(P\supseteq S\) is ideal when \(P=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)\). For closed convex relaxations \(P_1,P_2\supseteq S\), \(P_1\) is at least as strong as \(P_2\) when \(P_1\subseteq P_2\). In that case, for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\), \(\inf_{u\in P_1}c^\top u\geq\inf_{u\in P_2}c^\top u\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)\subseteq P\) for every closed convex relaxation \(P\supseteq S\), so the hull relaxation is strongest in this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex relaxations are ordered by set inclusion, and the closed convex hull is the strongest such relaxation and gives the strongest linear-minimization bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are closed convex sets containing \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_1\subseteq P_2\Rightarrow \inf_{u\in P_1}c^\top u\geq\inf_{u\in P_2}c^\top u\) for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\), and \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)\) is strongest among closed convex relaxations.

notation.meaning: combined vector (x,z) in the relaxation space

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sweep method for constructing a linear underestimator of a tree function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-sweep procedure over a layered computational tree; the node relations referenced as Eq. (18) are not included in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a tree function with levels \(k=1,\ldots,N\) and nodes \(i=1,\ldots,p_k\), the sweep method constructs a linear underestimator by: (1) performing a bottom-to-top sweep to obtain all node bounds \([\varphi_i^*,\varphi_i]\); (2) performing a top-to-bottom sweep to obtain the relations referenced as Eq. (18) at every level; and (3) performing a bottom-to-top sweep to obtain each \(L[\varphi_i^{(N-k)};S_i^{(N-k)}]\) as a linear function of \(x\) and \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sweep method constructs a linear underestimator in three passes: propagate node bounds upward, propagate the referenced node relations downward, and sweep upward again to express the nodewise underestimators as linear functions of x and u.
assumptions_latex: \text{The function has the stated layered tree representation.}
\text{The node relation referenced as Eq. (18) and the operator }L[\cdot;\cdot]\text{ are defined in the surrounding context.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L[\varphi_i^{(N-k)};S_i^{(N-k)}]\text{ is obtained as a linear function of }x\text{ and }u\text{ at the relevant nodes.}

children.title: Supporting Affine Minorants
children.top_down_role: Tangent-, subgradient-, and conjugate-generated affine lower models.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting Affine Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient and Fenchel-conjugate representations of global affine lower models for a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. If \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(g\in\partial f(\bar x)\), then \(a_{\bar x,g}(x)=f(\bar x)+g^\top(x-\bar x)\) satisfies \(a_{\bar x,g}(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), with equality at \(\bar x\). Equivalently, for every \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\), the affine function \(x\mapsto y^\top x-f^*(y)\) minorizes \(f\); it supports \(f\) at \(\bar x\) precisely when \(y\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex function is globally underestimated by each subgradient plane, equivalently by every affine function generated from its Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x)+g^\top(x-\bar x)\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\), and \(f(x)\geq y^\top x-f^*(y)\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of f at the support point

children.title: Chord-Interpolation Minorant Geometry
children.top_down_role: Chord- and vertex-interpolation-based lower models.

children.title: Secant Minorants
children.top_down_role: Lower models derived from chord geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The chord through two endpoint values is an affine minorant of a concave univariate function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave with \(a<b\). Its endpoint secant is \[s(x)=\frac{b-x}{b-a}\phi(a)+\frac{x-a}{b-a}\phi(b).\] Then \(s\) is affine, interpolates the endpoints, and satisfies \(s(x)\leq\phi(x)\) for every \(x\in[a,b]\). Thus the secant supplies a valid convex underestimator of \(\phi\) on the interval. The inequality reverses for convex \(\phi\), so an endpoint secant is generally an overestimator rather than a minorant in that regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a concave function, the endpoint secant lies below the graph; for a convex function, the inequality reverses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(a)=\phi(a)\), \(s(b)=\phi(b)\), and \(s(x)\leq\phi(x)\) for every \(x\in[a,b]\).

children.title: Interpolating Minorants
children.top_down_role: Lower models matching selected function values.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolating Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine interpolation at simplex vertices underestimates a concave function throughout the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_0,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be affinely independent, let \(T=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\), and let \(f:T\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave. Every \(x\in T\) has unique barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_i(x)\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)=1\) and \(x=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)v_i\). The affine interpolant \(\ell(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)f(v_i)\) obeys \(\ell(v_i)=f(v_i)\) and \(\ell(x)\leq f(x)\) throughout \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a simplex, affine interpolation of a concave function’s vertex values is a valid minorant that is exact at every vertex.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is real-valued and concave on their simplex \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(v_i)=f(v_i)\) for all \(i\), and \(\ell(x)\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\in T\).

notation.meaning: simplex generated by the interpolation vertices

children.title: Chord–Vertex Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric distinctions between chord-based plus vertex-based lower models.

knowledge_statements.title: Chord–Vertex Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric description of a simplex chord as the hyperplane through lifted vertex values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a simplex \(T=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\) and vertex data \(y_i\in\mathbb{R}\), the lifted points \((v_i,y_i)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) are affinely independent and determine a unique affine function \(\ell\) through \(\ell(v_i)=y_i\). Its graph over \(T\) is exactly \[\operatorname{conv}\{(v_i,y_i):i=0,\ldots,n\}=\{(x,\ell(x)):x\in T\}.\] If \(y_i=f(v_i)\) for a concave function \(f:T\to\mathbb{R}\), this chord facet lies on or below the graph of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted simplex vertices determine one affine chord facet; concavity places the function’s graph above that facet.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}\{(v_i,y_i)\}_{i=0}^n=\{(x,\ell(x)):x\in T\}\).

children.title: Maximum-of-Affine Models
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral convex lower models formed from collections of affine pieces.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-of-Affine Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite valid affine minorants combine into a convex polyhedral lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and suppose \(a_i^\top x+b_i\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define \[\widehat f_m(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\{a_i^\top x+b_i\},\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Then \(\widehat f_m\) is convex and polyhedral on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), satisfies \(\widehat f_m(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and has epigraph \[\operatorname{epi}\widehat f_m=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}:t\geq a_i^\top x+b_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Adding another valid affine minorant produces \(\widehat f_{m+1}\geq\widehat f_m\) pointwise while preserving validity on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global maximum of finitely many valid affine minorants is a convex polyhedral function that remains below the target on its domain, and adding valid pieces strengthens it pointwise.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i^\top x+b_i\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat f_m\) is convex and polyhedral on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\widehat f_m\leq f\) on \(X\), and adjoining a valid piece yields \(\widehat f_{m+1}\geq\widehat f_m\).

notation.meaning: maximum-of-affine lower model with m pieces

children.title: Successive Polyhedral Refinement
children.top_down_role: Adaptive strengthening of polyhedral underestimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Polyhedral Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive cutting-plane refinement of a convex objective’s polyhedral lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact convex set \(X\), a convex function \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), initial support pairs \((x_i,g_i)\) with \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), set \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\leq k}\{f(x_i)+g_i^\top(x-x_i)\}\). Compute \(x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}m_k(x)\), evaluate \(f(x_{k+1})\) and a subgradient \(g_{k+1}\), and append the resulting support. Maintain \(L_k=\min_Xm_k\) and the best sampled value \(U_k\). Stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent and certified interval \([L_k,U_k]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly minimize the current cutting-plane model, add a support there, and stop when the incumbent-to-lower-bound gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and has an available subgradient at each queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\leq m_{k+1}\leq f\), \(L_k\leq\min_X f\leq U_k\), and termination certifies \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: polyhedral lower model after k supports
current lower and incumbent upper bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Addition Rule for Convex Underestimators and Concave Overestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and curvature preservation when paired relaxations are propagated through binary addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex. For \(i=1,2\), suppose \(\underline f_i^X\) is a convex underestimator of \(f_i\) on \(X\) and \(\bar f_i^X\) is a concave overestimator of \(f_i\) on \(X\). Then \(\underline f_1^X+\underline f_2^X\) is a convex underestimator of \(f_1+f_2\) on \(X\), and \(\bar f_1^X+\bar f_2^X\) is a concave overestimator of \(f_1+f_2\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex set, the sum of convex underestimators is a convex underestimator of the function sum, and the sum of concave overestimators is a concave overestimator of that sum.
assumptions_latex: \underline f_i^X\text{ is convex and }\bar f_i^X\text{ is concave on }X,\qquad i=1,2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline f_1^X+\underline f_2^X\le f_1+f_2\le \bar f_1^X+\bar f_2^X\quad\text{on }X,\quad \underline f_1^X+\underline f_2^X\text{ is convex},\quad \bar f_1^X+\bar f_2^X\text{ is concave}.

source_evidence.locator: Lower Bounds / 4.12. Factorable functions / Proposition 4.110

children.title: McCormick Relaxation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Recursive propagation families for arithmetic operations and compositions.

children.title: Arithmetic-Operation Propagation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation propagation through sums, products, quotients, and related arithmetic structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic-Operation Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted propagation rules for sum, product, and sign-stable quotient nodes in a factorable expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each factorable-expression node with a lifted variable and valid finite interval bounds. For \(w=u+v\), impose \(w=u+v\). For \(w=uv\), with \(u\in[u^L,u^U]\) and \(v\in[v^L,v^U]\), impose \[w\geq u^Lv+v^Lu-u^Lv^L,\qquad w\geq u^Uv+v^Uu-u^Uv^U,\] \[w\leq u^Uv+v^Lu-u^Uv^L,\qquad w\leq u^Lv+v^Uu-u^Lv^U.\] For \(w=u/v\), assume \(0\notin[v^L,v^U]\), derive valid finite bounds \(w\in[w^L,w^U]\), and relax the equivalent equation \(u=wv\) by imposing the four McCormick inequalities for the product of \(w\) and \(v\), with \(u\) as the product variable. Recursing from the leaves to the root produces a valid lifted relaxation containing every exact evaluation over the prescribed bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate factorable relaxations using exact sum equations, McCormick product inequalities, and a sign-stable quotient reformulated and relaxed as a bounded product equation.
assumptions_latex: Every lifted operand has valid finite interval bounds.
For a quotient, \(0\notin[v^L,v^U]\) and valid finite bounds \([w^L,w^U]\) for the quotient variable are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursively constructed lifted set contains every exact evaluation of the factorable expression over the prescribed bounds.

notation.meaning: valid bounds for a quotient result when used in its product reformulation
lifted result of the current arithmetic node

children.title: Univariate Composition Propagation
children.top_down_role: Composition families organized by outer-function monotonicity and curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Composition Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex underestimator propagation selected by the outer function’s monotonicity and curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex and let \(g:X\to I\). If \(r^{\mathrm{cv}}:X\to I\) is convex with \(r^{\mathrm{cv}}\leq g\), and \(\phi:I\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and nondecreasing, then \(x\mapsto\phi(r^{\mathrm{cv}}(x))\) is convex and underestimates \(\phi(g(x))\). If \(r^{\mathrm{cc}}:X\to I\) is concave with \(r^{\mathrm{cc}}\geq g\), and \(\phi\) is convex and nonincreasing, then \(x\mapsto\phi(r^{\mathrm{cc}}(x))\) is likewise a convex underestimator. Thus monotonicity determines whether an inner underestimator or overestimator must be propagated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex increasing outer function uses an inner convex underestimator; a convex decreasing outer function uses an inner concave overestimator.
assumptions_latex: All displayed inner functions take values in \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\circ r^{\mathrm{cv}}\leq\phi\circ g\) in the nondecreasing case, and \(\phi\circ r^{\mathrm{cc}}\leq\phi\circ g\) in the nonincreasing case.

notation.meaning: convex underestimator of the inner function
concave overestimator of the inner function

children.title: Multivariate Composition Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Extensions to multivariate outer mappings and jointly relaxed inner functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Composition Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise monotonicity selects inner relaxations for a convex multivariate outer mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex, let \(g_i:X\to I_i\), and let \(\Phi:I_1\times\cdots\times I_m\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Partition coordinates into \(P\), where \(\Phi\) is nondecreasing, and \(N\), where it is nonincreasing. For \(i\in P\), choose a convex \(r_i\leq g_i\); for \(i\in N\), choose a concave \(r_i\geq g_i\). Provided \(r(x)\) lies in the domain of \(\Phi\), the function \(R(x)=\Phi(r_1(x),\ldots,r_m(x))\) is convex and satisfies \(R(x)\leq\Phi(g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex multivariate outer function, coordinate monotonicity determines which inner under- or overrelaxation yields a convex lower model.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is convex and has the stated coordinatewise monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is convex on \(X\) and \(R(x)\leq\Phi(g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))\) for all \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: selected inner relaxation for coordinate i

children.title: Subgradient Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient chain rule for monotonic convex multivariate composition relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the multivariate composition construction \(R(x)=\Phi(r_1(x),\ldots,r_m(x))\). Suppose \(\Phi\) is differentiable at \(r(\bar x)\). For every nondecreasing coordinate \(i\), select \(s_i\in\partial r_i(\bar x)\); for every nonincreasing coordinate \(i\), select a supergradient \(s_i\in\partial^+r_i(\bar x)\). Then \[p=\sum_{i=1}^m \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial y_i}(r(\bar x))s_i\] belongs to \(\partial R(\bar x)\). Hence local sensitivity information can be propagated through the relaxation graph while respecting the same monotonicity choices used to establish convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite relaxation’s subgradient is obtained by weighting inner sub- or supergradients with outer partial derivatives of the appropriate signs.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) satisfies the hypotheses of the multivariate composition rule.
The required subgradients and supergradients exist at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\partial R(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of an inner convex relaxation
concave superdifferential of an inner concave relaxation

children.title: Original-Space Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Direct propagation without explicit variables for every intermediate expression.

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) has a finite factorable expression over a box \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
Every primitive operation is supplied with valid convex and concave relaxation rules on its propagated operand bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)\le f(x)\le f^{\mathrm{cc}}(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with both relaxations expressed only in \(x\).

notation.meaning: Recursively propagated convex and concave relaxations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: recursive factorable-function relaxation validity follows by induction over the expression graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional relaxation in the original variables, without explicit intermediate-variable constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Evaluate the expression graph of \(f\) recursively while retaining, at every node, convex and concave relaxation functions of the original vector \(x\). If each primitive rule preserves enclosure on its operand bounds, the root functions satisfy
\[f^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)\le f(x)\le f^{\mathrm{cc}}(x)\qquad(x\in X).\]
Thus \(f^{\mathrm{cv}}\) is a convex underestimator represented directly in the original space; intermediate node values are substituted symbolically rather than introduced as independent optimization variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursive primitive relaxations produce convex and concave bounds expressed directly in the original variables, without adding variables for intermediate expressions.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited alphaBB section does not specifically support original-space factorable relaxation propagation. The intended primitive rules must preserve convexity or concavity as well as enclosure; the statement's abbreviated condition is ambiguous.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Lifted expression graphs exposing intermediate nonlinear operations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is represented by a finite directed acyclic expression graph.
Each noninput node has a valid convex outer relaxation of the graph of its primitive operation over known operand bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted convex system contains every exact evaluation of \(f\), so minimizing its output variable gives a valid lower bound on \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary value assigned to expression-graph node v.
Convex outer relaxation for the primitive relation at node v.
Root node representing the objective value.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: lifted expression-graph relaxations are valid because every exact primitive tuple remains in its outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted formulation obtained by convexifying individual relations in an expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce one variable \(z_v\) for every noninput node \(v\), and impose \((z_v,z_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})\in R_v\), where \(R_v\) is a convex outer relaxation of the corresponding primitive graph. The lifted relaxation is
\[\mathcal R=\{(x,z):x\in X,\ (z_v,z_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})\in R_v\text{ for every noninput }v\}.\]
Every exact evaluation vector belongs to \(\mathcal R\). Consequently, if \(r\) is the root node, then \(\inf_{(x,z)\in\mathcal R}z_r\le\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce variables for intermediate expression nodes and replace each exact primitive relation by a convex outer relaxation; the lifted optimum is a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifted outer-relaxation construction is sound and fits the container, but the cited alphaBB section does not specifically support expression-graph auxiliary-variable relaxations.

Unroll the updates \(y_{k+1}=\Phi_k(x,y_k)\) into a finite computational graph and propagate bounds together with convex and concave relaxations through every primitive operation. Applying the same rules to the terminal map \(F(x)=\psi(y_K)\) yields functions satisfying

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B=\prod_{i=1}^n[x_i^L,x_i^U] and \mathcal L(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^L-x_i)(x_i^U-x_i), with \alpha\geq0. Then \max_{x\in B}\bigl(f(x)-\mathcal L(x)\bigr)=\frac{\alpha}{4}\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^U-x_i^L)^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative alpha, the largest gap between the original function and the uniform alphaBB underestimator is alpha divided by four times the sum of the squared box widths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{x\in B}\bigl(f(x)-\mathcal L(x)\bigr)=\frac{\alpha}{4}\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i^U-x_i^L)^2

children.title: Spectral Curvature Bounds
children.top_down_role: Curvature certification using eigenvalue information.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Curvature Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isotropic alphaBB correction certified by a uniform minimum-eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[l,u]\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\). Suppose \(\underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\) for every \(x\in B\). For every \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda/2\}\), the function
\[f_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-l_i)(x_i-u_i)\]
is convex on \(B\) and satisfies \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the Hessian eigenvalues are uniformly bounded below by lambda-bar on the box, every alpha at least the maximum of zero and minus lambda-bar divided by two defines a convex alphaBB underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(B=[l,u]\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda/2\}\), the function \(f_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\) and satisfies \(f_\alpha\le f\) there.

notation.meaning: Uniform spectral lower bound for the Hessian.

children.title: Gershgorin-Type Curvature Bounds
children.top_down_role: Curvature certification derived from interval Hessian structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Gershgorin-Type Curvature Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unscaled Gershgorin certification from a symmetric interval Hessian enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[l,u]\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f\in C^2(B)\), and suppose \(\nabla^2_{ij}f(x)\in[\underline H_{ij},\overline H_{ij}]\) for every \(x\in B\). Define
\[m_{ij}=\max\{|\underline H_{ij}|,|\overline H_{ij}|\}\quad(i\ne j),\qquad \underline\lambda_G=\min_{1\le i\le n}\left(\underline H_{ii}-\sum_{j\ne i}m_{ij}\right).\]
Then \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge\underline\lambda_G\) for every \(x\in B\). For every \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda_G/2\}\),
\[f_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-l_i)(x_i-u_i)\]
is a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interval Hessian gives the stated Gershgorin lower bound on every Hessian eigenvalue; any alpha at least the maximum of zero and minus half that bound defines a convex alphaBB underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(B=[l,u]\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(f\in C^2(B)\), and interval bounds \(\nabla^2_{ij}f(x)\in[\underline H_{ij},\overline H_{ij}]\) hold on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline\lambda_G\le\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\) on \(B\), so every \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\lambda_G/2\}\) yields a convex alphaBB underestimator.

notation.meaning: Maximum absolute magnitude admitted by an off-diagonal Hessian interval.
Gershgorin lower bound on every Hessian eigenvalue.

children.title: Anisotropic Curvature-Correction Variants
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-scaled, anisotropic, and matrix-valued curvature corrections.

children.title: Scaled Curvature Corrections
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-scaled curvature modifications for underestimator strength or conditioning.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\mu/2\}\), the scaled correction defines a convex underestimator on \(B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: congruence scaling reduces the convexity test to a minimum-eigenvalue bound for the scaled Hessian.
A source specifically covering scaled alphaBB corrections is required.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal rescaling of separable alphaBB curvature corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\underline\mu/2\}\), define
\[f_{\alpha,D}(x)=f(x)+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^n d_i(x_i-l_i)(x_i-u_i).\]
The correction is nonpositive throughout \(B\). Its Hessian satisfies
\[D^{-1/2}\nabla^2 f_{\alpha,D}(x)D^{-1/2}=D^{-1/2}\nabla^2f(x)D^{-1/2}+2\alpha I\succeq0.\]
Thus \(f_{\alpha,D}\) is convex and obeys \(f_{\alpha,D}(x)\le f(x)\) on \(B\). The scaling may redistribute curvature compensation among coordinates without changing validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal scaling redistributes the separable correction; a spectral bound for the scaled Hessian certifies convexity and underestimation.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Curvature Corrections

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled spectral certificate is internally correct and matches the leaf, but no inspectable source supports its identification as a scaled alphaBB variant.

children.title: Nondiagonal Curvature Corrections
children.top_down_role: Curvature modifications using cross-coordinate matrix structure.

assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a convex compact set and \(f\in C^2(B)\).
\(q(x)=x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) has \(A=A^T\) with at least one nonzero off-diagonal entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two displayed inequalities are sufficient for \(f+q\) to be a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pointwise nonpositivity gives underestimation and positive-semidefinite corrected Hessian gives convexity.
A canonical construction and source for nondiagonal alphaBB corrections are still required.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General validity conditions for a quadratic correction containing cross-coordinate terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nondiagonal quadratic correction \(q(x)=x^TAx+b^Tx+c\) is valid whenever
\[q(x)\le0\qquad(x\in B)\]
and
\[\nabla^2f(x)+2A\succeq0\qquad(x\in B).\]
Under these conditions the corrected function \(f_q=f+q\) satisfies \(f_q(x)\le f(x)\) and is convex on \(B\). Unlike a separable alphaBB correction, off-diagonal entries of \(A\) couple coordinates; consequently, nonpositivity of \(q\) on the entire domain must be certified separately and does not follow merely from \(A\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic correction with cross terms is valid when it is nonpositive on the domain and its Hessian addition makes the objective convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Nondiagonal Curvature Corrections

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed conditions are sufficient, but a source is required to establish this general cross-term construction within the intended nondiagonal alphaBB regime.

children.title: Matrix-Valued Variants
children.top_down_role: Anisotropic corrections represented through full or structured matrices.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_S(x)=f(x)+(x-m)^TS(x-m)-\rho\) is a convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: subtracting the maximum of a convex quadratic over the box makes the matrix correction nonpositive.
A source connecting this general matrix construction to named alphaBB variants is required.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A full positive-semidefinite matrix correction normalized to remain nonpositive on the box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[f_S(x)=f(x)+(x-m)^TS(x-m)-\rho.\]
The definition of \(\rho\) ensures \((x-m)^TS(x-m)-\rho\le0\) for every \(x\in B\), so \(f_S\le f\) on \(B\). Furthermore,
\[\nabla^2 f_S(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+2S\succeq0.\]
Hence \(f_S\) is a convex underestimator. Allowing a full matrix \(S\), rather than a scalar or diagonal matrix, permits curvature compensation along coupled directions, subject to computing or bounding the normalization constant \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite matrix can compensate coupled negative curvature after its quadratic correction is shifted to remain nonpositive over the box.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Valued Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is mathematically sufficient, but it is a certificate or condition rather than a representation. A source is also needed to connect this normalized full-matrix construction to the intended alphaBB variants.

children.title: Ambient-Domain Curvature
children.top_down_role: Curvature certification over a containing box or convex region.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(D\) is convex, and \(f\in C^2(D)\).
A twice differentiable correction \(q\) satisfies \(q(x)\le0\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)+\nabla^2q(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f+q\) is a convex underestimator on \(D\), hence a valid lower model of \(f\) on \(F\).

notation.meaning: Containing convex region used for certification.
Feasible subset of the ambient region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature and underestimation certified over a convex set containing the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=f+q\). The conditions
\[q(x)\le0\quad\text{and}\quad\nabla^2g(x)\succeq0\qquad(x\in D)\]
certify respectively that \(g(x)\le f(x)\) and that \(g\) is convex throughout the ambient region \(D\). Since \(F\subseteq D\), the same pointwise inequality holds on \(F\), and therefore
\[\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}g(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\]
Ambient-domain certification is sufficient but may require compensating curvature in directions or locations irrelevant to feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certifying nonpositivity and convexity on a convex region containing the feasible set yields a valid, potentially conservative, constrained lower model.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambient-Domain Curvature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ambient-domain implication is standard, but the cited box-constrained alphaBB section does not specifically support the generalized constrained-domain statement over arbitrary convex D and correction q.

children.title: Feasible-Region Curvature
children.top_down_role: Curvature certification restricted to feasible geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty convex set and \(f,q\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restriction \((f+q)|_F\) is convex and underestimates \(f|_F\).

notation.meaning: Linear space of feasible chord directions.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Hessian positivity along feasible chord directions characterizes convexity of a smooth restriction to a convex affine hull.
A constrained-curvature source addressing lower-dimensional feasible geometry is required.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth curvature certification restricted to a convex feasible set and its chord directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=f+q\). If
\[q(x)\le0\qquad(x\in F)\]
and
\[v^T\nabla^2g(x)v\ge0\qquad(x\in F,\ v\in\operatorname{lin}(F-F)),\]
then the restriction \(g|_F\) is convex and satisfies \(g(x)\le f(x)\) for every feasible \(x\). Only curvature along directions in the affine hull of \(F\) is relevant. Thus feasible-region certification can accept a correction rejected by an ambient full-space positive-semidefiniteness test, especially when \(F\) is lower-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex feasible set, only curvature along feasible chord directions must be nonnegative; this can yield tighter corrections than ambient certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Region Curvature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-direction Hessian condition is mathematically appropriate for a smooth restriction to a convex set, but this lower-dimensional constrained-curvature formulation lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Constraint-Aggregated Underestimators
children.top_down_role: Objective and constraint combinations producing strengthened convex lower models.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and \(F=\{x\in D:g_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The multipliers satisfy \(\lambda_j\ge0\), and \(L_\lambda=f+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j\) is convex on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_\lambda(x)\le f(x)\) on \(F\), and \(\inf_{x\in D}L_\lambda(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible region defined by inequality constraints.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonnegative aggregation of nonpositive feasible constraint residuals gives a pointwise objective underestimator.
A source specifically treating convexified constraint aggregation in global optimization is desirable.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian-type aggregation of inequality constraints into a convex objective lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(x\in F\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define
\[L_\lambda(x)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j(x).\]
Feasibility gives \(\sum_j\lambda_jg_j(x)\le0\), hence \(L_\lambda(x)\le f(x)\) on \(F\). If \(L_\lambda\) is convex on \(D\), it is a convex lower model incorporating both objective and constraint curvature, and
\[\inf_{x\in D}L_\lambda(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\]
Selecting multipliers that preserve convexity while increasing this lower bound strengthens the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding nonnegative multiples of feasible inequality residuals underestimates the objective; when the aggregate is convex, its minimum supplies a strengthened lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Aggregated Underestimators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonnegative constraint aggregation and lower-bound inequality are correct and fit the leaf, but the nontrivial global-optimization construction has no inspectable citation.

children.title: DC Decomposition Families
children.top_down_role: Alternative canonical, noncanonical, separable, and composite DC representations.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite-dimensional DC representations relevant to constructing convex minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex. A DC representation of \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is an identity \(f=g-h\) on \(D\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on \(D\). If \(q\) is convex on \(D\), then \[f=(g+q)-(h+q),\] so a DC function generally has many decompositions. Structured subfamilies arise by requiring \(g\) and \(h\) to be separable, polynomial, or composite convex functions. These representations are functionally equivalent but need not produce identical minorants after one component is replaced by a tractable bounding model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC function admits many equivalent convex-minus-convex representations, including structured separable, polynomial, and composite families that can induce different relaxations.
assumptions_latex: g,h,q\text{ are finite and convex on }D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=(g+q)-(h+q)\text{ on }D

notation.meaning: a difference-of-convex representation of the target function
a common convex term added to both components

children.title: Support-Based DC Minorants
children.top_down_role: Convex minorants obtained from supporting models of the subtracted convex component.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Based DC Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex minorants obtained by upper-bounding the subtracted DC component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\) on a convex set \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with \(g\) and \(h\) convex. Suppose an affine function \(a(x)=\alpha^\top x+\beta\) satisfies \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Then \(m=g-a\) is convex on \(D\) and \[m(x)=g(x)-a(x)\le g(x)-h(x)=f(x)\qquad(x\in D).\] Thus any valid affine upper supporting model of the subtracted component produces a convex minorant. On a simplex, the affine interpolant of \(h\) through the vertices is such an upper model by convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the subtracted convex component by a valid affine upper model yields a convex underestimator of the DC function.
assumptions_latex: a\text{ is affine and }a\ge h\text{ on }D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m:=g-a\text{ is convex on }D\text{ and }m\le f\text{ on }D

notation.meaning: affine upper model of the subtracted convex component

children.title: DC Decomposition Strength
children.top_down_role: Dependence of minorant quality on the chosen DC representation.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise ordering criterion for minorants induced by DC decompositions and affine upper models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex. For \(k\in\{1,2\}\), let \(f=g_k-h_k\) on \(D\), where \(g_k\) and \(h_k\) are convex on \(D\), and let \(a_k\) be affine with \(a_k\ge h_k\) on \(D\). Define \(m_k=g_k-a_k\). The first minorant is at least as strong as the second exactly when \(m_1(x)\ge m_2(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). In particular, for a fixed decomposition \(f=g-h\), if valid affine upper models satisfy \(h\le a_1\le a_2\) on \(D\), then \[g-a_1\ge g-a_2\quad\text{on }D.\] Consequently, the smaller valid upper model gives the tighter convex minorant and satisfies \(\inf_{x\in D}(g(x)-a_1(x))\ge\inf_{x\in D}(g(x)-a_2(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC minorant strength is determined pointwise: for a fixed decomposition, the smaller valid affine upper model of the subtracted component yields the stronger minorant and no smaller minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty and convex}
a_k\text{ is affine and }a_k\ge h_k\text{ on }D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_1\ge m_2\text{ on }D\Longrightarrow \inf_{x\in D}m_1(x)\ge\inf_{x\in D}m_2(x)

notation.meaning: minorant induced by decomposition and upper model k
valid affine upper model of the subtracted convex component
lower bound obtained by minimizing the minorant over the domain

children.title: Reformulation–Linearization Technique
children.top_down_role: Systematic lifted-product and linear-relaxation families.

knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation–Linearization Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-factor RLT relaxation for polynomial constraints on a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given polynomial constraints on \(x\in[l,u]\) and a relaxation degree \(d\), form valid products of original constraints with bound factors \((x_i-l_i)\) and \((u_i-x_i)\), retaining products of total degree at most \(d\). Introduce one lifted variable \(y_\alpha\) for every monomial \(x^\alpha\) that occurs, impose \(y_0=1\), and replace each occurrence of \(x^\alpha\) by \(y_\alpha\). The resulting linear equalities and inequalities define an RLT polyhedral relaxation. Solve its linear objective; its optimum is a lower bound for minimization. Stop when the prescribed degree or bound-gap criterion is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RLT multiplies constraints by valid bound factors, lifts resulting monomials, and linearizes them to obtain a polyhedral lower-bounding relaxation.
assumptions_latex: d\in\mathbb N\text{ is the selected relaxation degree}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
S\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R_d)\quad\text{and}
\quad\min_{R_d}c^\top y\le\min_{x\in S}f(x)

notation.meaning: lifted variable representing the monomial with multi-index alpha

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the proposed RLT algorithm does not precisely specify which constraint products are generated or how the polynomial objective is represented by the stated linear objective. These choices materially affect validity and degree conventions.

children.title: Extended Convex Formulations
children.top_down_role: Lifted convex models and their projections into the original space.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Convex Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex underestimators represented through lifted epigraph relaxations and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), let \(m\in\mathbb N\), and let \(Z(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty for every \(x\in D\). Define the exact lifted epigraph \[E=\{(x,z,t):x\in D,\ z\in Z(x),\ t\ge f(x)\}.\] Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m+1}\) be convex and upper-closed in \(t\), with \(E\subseteq Q\), and assume \(P:=\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}Q\) is closed. Define \[\phi(x)=\inf\{t:\exists z\in\mathbb R^m\text{ such that }(x,z,t)\in Q\}.\] Then \(\phi\) is convex on its effective domain, \(\operatorname{epi}\phi=P\), and \(\phi(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Thus eliminating auxiliary variables from a lifted convex outer approximation yields a convex minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a lifted convex, upper-closed outer approximation of an exact epigraph yields the epigraph of a convex underestimator, provided the projection is closed.
assumptions_latex: m\in\mathbb N\text{ and }\varnothing\ne Z(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^m\text{ for every }x\in D
Q\text{ is convex and upper-closed in }t
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}\phi=\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}Q\quad\text{and}\quad\phi\le f\text{ on }D

children.title: Disjunctive Convexification
