knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex-hull representation for a union of compact convex regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\in\mathbb N\) and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_r\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex sets. Define \[H=\left\{(x,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\lambda):x=\sum_{i=1}^r x^i,\ \sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i=1,\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ x^i\in\lambda_i C_i\ \text{for all }i\right\}.\] Then \[\operatorname{proj}_x H=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^r C_i\right).\] Here \(\lambda_i C_i=\{\lambda_i z:z\in C_i\}\), including \(0C_i=\{0\}\). Thus \(H\) is an exact lifted convexification of the finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite union of nonempty compact convex regions has an exact lifted convex-hull representation using nonnegative region weights and scaled regional copies.
assumptions_latex: C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, compact, and convex for every }i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x H=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^r C_i\right)

notation.meaning: nonnegative weight assigned to region i
scaled regional copy of the decision vector

children.title: Piecewise Convexification
children.top_down_role: Region-indexed convexification of piecewise nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convex minorant assembled from local convex epigraph models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\in\mathbb N\), let \(D=\bigcup_{i=1}^rD_i\), where each \(D_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\). For each \(i\), let \(u_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\) be convex and satisfy \(u_i(x)\le f(x)\) on \(D_i\). Define \[Q=\operatorname{clconv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^r\{(x,t):x\in D_i,\ t\ge u_i(x)\}\right),\qquad u(x)=\inf\{t:(x,t)\in Q\}.\] Then \(u\) is convex on \(\operatorname{conv}D\) and satisfies \(u(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying the union of regional underestimator epigraphs yields a global convex underestimator over the union of the regions.
assumptions_latex: D=\bigcup_{i=1}^rD_i\text{ with each }D_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ nonempty, compact, and convex}
u_i:D_i\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex and }u_i\le f\text{ on }D_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\text{ is convex on }\operatorname{conv}D\quad\text{and}\quad u\le f\text{ on }D

notation.meaning: closed convex hull of the regional epigraphs

children.title: Hull-Strengthened Regional Models
children.top_down_role: Regional formulations designed to approach or attain disjunctive hull strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Hull-Strengthened Regional Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance of regional convex-hull relaxations over looser common relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a nonempty finite index set, let \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) for \(i\in I\), and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be convex with \(\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i\subseteq Q\). Define \(H=\operatorname{clconv}(\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i)\). Then \(H\subseteq Q\), and for every \(c\in\mathbb R^p\), \[\inf_{z\in H}c^\top z\ge\inf_{z\in Q}c^\top z.\] If \(H\subsetneq Q\) and some point of \(Q\setminus H\) is strongly separated from \(H\), then strict improvement occurs for a corresponding linear objective. Thus replacing the common relaxation by the regional closed convex hull cannot weaken a linear minimization bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a common relaxation by the closed convex hull of its regional feasible sets cannot worsen any linear minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: I\text{ is a nonempty finite index set}
Q\subseteq\mathbb R^p\text{ is convex and }\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i\subseteq Q
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\subseteq Q\Longrightarrow \inf_{z\in H}c^\top z\ge\inf_{z\in Q}c^\top z\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^p

notation.meaning: closed convex hull of all regional sets

children.title: Formulation-Dependent Strength
children.top_down_role: Variation in relaxation strength among algebraically equivalent formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation-Dependent Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation dominance for algebraically equivalent lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Let two exact lifted formulations \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) satisfy \(\operatorname{proj}_xF_1=\operatorname{proj}_xF_2=S\), and let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be convex relaxations with \(F_k\subseteq R_k\) for \(k\in\{1,2\}\). Define \(X_k=\operatorname{proj}_xR_k\). Algebraic equivalence of the exact formulations does not imply \(X_1=X_2\). If \(X_1\subseteq X_2\), then for every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\inf_{x\in X_1}c^\top x\ge\inf_{x\in X_2}c^\top x.\] Thus formulation 1 is at least as strong as formulation 2 for linear minimization objectives; incomparable projected relaxations can be stronger for different objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent exact formulations can yield different relaxations; inclusion of their projected relaxed sets determines uniform dominance for linear minimization objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_1\subseteq X_2\Longrightarrow\inf_{x\in X_1}c^\top x\ge\inf_{x\in X_2}c^\top x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n

notation.meaning: projection of the relaxed formulation into the original variables

children.title: Convex Polynomial Minorants

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Polynomial Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial underestimators satisfying domain validity and convexity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\). A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) is a convex polynomial minorant of \(f\) on \(D\) if \(p\) is convex on \(D\) and \[p(x)\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in D.\] If \(D\) has nonempty interior, convexity of the polynomial on \(D\) is equivalent to \(\nabla^2p(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}D\). For lower-dimensional domains, convexity is imposed directly on \(D\). Every such minorant satisfies \(\inf_{x\in D}p(x)\le\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex polynomial minorant is a polynomial that is convex on the domain and nowhere exceeds the target function there.
assumptions_latex: D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\le f\text{ on }D\quad\text{and}\quad p\text{ is convex on }D

k\geq\max\{\lceil d/2\rceil,\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil\},

the semidefinite program \(\mathbf P_{dk}\), defined by truncated quadratic-module certificates for \(f-h\geq0\) on \(\mathbf B\) and \(\mathbf Th\geq0\) on \(\mathbf B\times\mathbf U\), has an optimal solution \(f_{dk}\in\mathbb R[x]_d\).

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf P_{dk}\) is the stated truncated quadratic-module SDP approximation of the degree-\(d\) convex polynomial minorant problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists f_{dk}\in\mathbb R[x]_d\) attaining the optimum of \(\mathbf P_{dk}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interval correction certificate for a polynomial underestimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous certification of a polynomial lower model over a box using an interval enclosure of its residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X=[\underline{x},\bar{x}], let p be a polynomial on X, and define \delta(x)=f(x)-p(x). If interval arithmetic produces [\underline{\delta},\bar{\delta}] satisfying \delta(x)\in[\underline{\delta},\bar{\delta}] for every x\in X, then \underline{p}(x):=p(x)+\underline{\delta} is a rigorous polynomial underestimator of f on X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If interval arithmetic encloses every residual value f(x)−p(x) on a box, adding the enclosure's lower endpoint to p gives a certified polynomial lower bound for f throughout that box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in X,\quad \underline{p}(x):=p(x)+\underline{\delta}\le f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral-best degree-at-most-d convex polynomial minorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the integral-optimal convex polynomial underestimation problem on the unit box, its Hessian-polynomial convexity representation, and its L1 interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf B=[0,1]^n\), \(\mathbf U=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\|y\|^2\leq1\}\), \(\mathbf S=\mathbf B\times\mathbf U\), and \((\mathbf Th)(x,y)=y^T\nabla^2h(x)y\). For \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), define
\[
\rho_d=\inf_{h\in\mathbb R[x]_d}\left\{\int_{\mathbf B}(f-h)\,dx:f-h\geq0\text{ on }\mathbf B,\ \mathbf Th\geq0\text{ on }\mathbf S\right\}.
\]
The condition \(\mathbf Th\geq0\) on \(\mathbf S\) is equivalent to convexity of \(h\) on \(\mathbf B\). For every feasible \(h\),
\[
\int_{\mathbf B}(f-h)\,dx=\int_{\mathbf B}|f-h|\,dx=\|f-h\|_{L^1(\mathbf B)}.
\]
If \(\deg f\leq d\) and \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbf B\), then \(\rho_d=0\) and \(h=f\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among degree-at-most-d convex polynomials lying below f on the unit box, the problem minimizes the integral gap. Convexity is equivalently expressed by nonnegativity of the Hessian quadratic form on the box times the unit ball, and the integral gap equals the L1 error. If f itself is convex and has degree at most d, it is optimal with value zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf B=[0,1]^n\), \(\mathbf U=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\|y\|^2\leq1\}\), and \(\mathbf S=\mathbf B\times\mathbf U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d=\inf\{\|f-h\|_{L^1(\mathbf B)}:h\leq f\text{ on }\mathbf B,\ h\text{ convex on }\mathbf B,\ \deg h\leq d\}\); if \(\deg f\leq d\) and \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbf B\), then \(\rho_d=0\) with optimizer \(h=f\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of the SDP hierarchy for convex polynomial minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone optimal-value convergence and optimality of accumulation points for the SOS-SDP hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\rho_d\) be the optimal value of the degree-\(d\) convex polynomial minorant problem. For each admissible order \(k\), let \(\rho_{dk}\) be the optimal value of its SDP relaxation and let \(f_{dk}\in\mathbb R[x]_d\) be any optimal solution. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbf B}f\,dx-\rho_{dk}\downarrow\rho_d,
\qquad
\|f-f_{dk}\|_{L^1(\mathbf B)}\downarrow\rho_d
\quad\text{as }k\to\infty.
\]
Moreover, every accumulation point \(\varphi^*\in\mathbb R[x]_d\) of \((f_{dk})\) is an optimal solution of the original problem, and there is a subsequence \((f_{dk_i})\) converging pointwise to \(\varphi^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SDP hierarchy's underestimation errors decrease to the optimal L1 error. Every accumulation point of its optimal polynomial underestimators solves the original problem, and a subsequence converges pointwise to that optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_d\) is the optimal value of the degree-\(d\) convex polynomial minorant problem.
For each admissible \(k\), \(\rho_{dk}\) and \(f_{dk}\in\mathbb R[x]_d\) are respectively the optimal value and an optimal solution of \(\mathbf P_{dk}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\int_{\mathbf B}f\,dx-\rho_{dk}\downarrow\rho_d\), \(\|f-f_{dk}\|_{L^1(\mathbf B)}\downarrow\rho_d\), and every accumulation point of \((f_{dk})\) is an optimizer of the original problem and the pointwise limit of a subsequence.

knowledge_statements.title: SOS-Certified Polynomial Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOS certificates for polynomial underestimation and global convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,p,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) and define \(D=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Suppose there exist sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that \[f-p=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\] and suppose \(y^\top\nabla^2p(x)y\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial in \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\). These conditions certify that \(p(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\) and that \(p\) is globally convex. Consequently, \(p\) is a convex polynomial minorant of \(f\) on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS identities certify nonnegativity of the underestimation gap on a basic semialgebraic domain and global convexity of the polynomial minorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\le f\text{ on }D\quad\text{and}\quad p\text{ is globally convex}

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Underestimator Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance and nested-class comparison of polynomial and alternative minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(u,v:D\to\mathbb R\) be convex minorants of \(f\). The minorant \(u\) is at least as strong as \(v\) pointwise when \(u(x)\ge v(x)\) for every \(x\in D\); in that case, \[\inf_{x\in D}u(x)\ge\inf_{x\in D}v(x).\] If admissible polynomial-minorant classes satisfy \(\mathcal P_d\subseteq\mathcal P_{d+1}\) and each class is optimized by maximizing the same linear fitting functional \(L(p)\), then \[\sup_{p\in\mathcal P_d}L(p)\le\sup_{p\in\mathcal P_{d+1}}L(p).\] Construction labels such as polynomial, curvature-based, or primitive-wise alone imply no universal dominance; comparisons require pointwise ordering or a specified quality metric together with computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimators compare by pointwise dominance or a declared metric. Maximizing the same fitting functional over nested polynomial classes gives monotone nondecreasing optimal values, while construction labels alone imply no ordering.
assumptions_latex: u,v:D\to\mathbb R\text{ are convex and satisfy }u,v\le f\text{ on }D
L\text{ is the same maximized linear fitting functional for all compared classes}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\ge v\text{ on }D\Longrightarrow\inf_{x\in D}u(x)\ge\inf_{x\in D}v(x)

notation.meaning: admissible polynomial-minorant class of level or degree d
fixed linear fitting functional maximized over each admissible class

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual L1 dominance over the alphaBB underestimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison on a common box between an optimal degree-bounded convex polynomial underestimator from problem (15.4) and a strictly convex alphaBB underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be a nonconvex polynomial, let \(f_{dk}\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_d\) be an optimal solution of problem (15.4), and let \(\mathcal L\) be the alphaBB underestimator from (15.7) on \(B\). If \(\nabla^2\mathcal L(\mathbf x)\succ0\) for every \(\mathbf x\in B\), then, for all sufficiently large \(k\),
\[
\lVert f-f_{dk}\rVert_{L^1(B)}\leq \lVert f-\mathcal L\rVert_{L^1(B)},
\qquad
\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^1(B)}:=\int_B|f(\mathbf x)-g(\mathbf x)|\,d\mathbf x.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the alphaBB underestimator has a positive-definite Hessian everywhere on the box, then for all sufficiently large k the optimal degree-d polynomial underestimator from problem (15.4) has no greater integrated absolute error than the alphaBB underestimator.
assumptions_latex: f_{dk}\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_d\text{ is an optimal solution of problem (15.4)}
\mathcal L\text{ is the alphaBB underestimator from (15.7) on }B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k_0\ \forall k\geq k_0:\quad \int_B|f(\mathbf x)-f_{dk}(\mathbf x)|\,d\mathbf x\leq\int_B|f(\mathbf x)-\mathcal L(\mathbf x)|\,d\mathbf x.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise representation of a nonempty finite box used to localize a global optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite vectors \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\), the associated box is
\[B=[\ell,u]:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n\}=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i].\]
Thus the pair \((\ell,u)\) is an exact coordinatewise representation of \(B\); a coordinate is fixed precisely when \(\ell_i=u_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite box is exactly the Cartesian product of its coordinate intervals; equal lower and upper bounds fix the corresponding variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=[\ell,u]=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate-Expression Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound interval bounds for nodes of a factorable expression evaluated over a localization box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an expression graph have variable leaves \(x_i\), and let each internal node \(v\) represent \(z_v=\phi_v(z_{p_1},\ldots,z_{p_k})\). A propagated interval \(I_v=[L_v,U_v]\) is valid on a box \(B\) when
\[\{z_v(x):x\in B\}\subseteq I_v.\]
Starting with \(I_{x_i}=[\ell_i,u_i]\), sound interval extensions \(\Phi_v\) produce valid bounds recursively by \(I_v=\Phi_v(I_{p_1},\ldots,I_{p_k})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each expression node receives an interval containing all values it can attain on the box, computed recursively from sound interval extensions.
assumptions_latex: Every primitive \(\phi_v\) has a sound interval extension \(\Phi_v\) on the relevant operand intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_v(B)\subseteq I_v\) for every expression node \(v\).

children.title: Bound-Propagation Quality
children.top_down_role: Effects of range sharpness on downstream relaxation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Propagation Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two checkable quality criteria for interval propagation: enclosure excess and convergence under box contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an intermediate expression \(z_v\) on a box \(B\), let \(I_v(B)=[L_v(B),U_v(B)]\) be a sound propagated interval and let \(R_v(B)=[\inf_{x\in B}z_v(x),\sup_{x\in B}z_v(x)]\) be its exact range hull. Its excess width is
\[e_v(B):=\operatorname{wid}(I_v(B))-\operatorname{wid}(R_v(B))\ge0.\]
Propagation is range-convergent at \(\bar x\) if \(e_v(B_k)\to0\) for every nested sequence \(B_k\downarrow\{\bar x\}\). Smaller excess width means a tighter valid enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation quality is measured by width beyond the exact range hull; range convergence requires this excess to vanish as boxes shrink to a point.
assumptions_latex: \(z_v\) is bounded on every considered box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_v(B)\ge0\), and range convergence at \(\bar x\) means \(e_v(B_k)\to0\) whenever \(B_k\downarrow\{\bar x\}\).

notation.meaning: exact interval hull of the expression range

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The excess-width metric and convergence definition are coherent, but no source supports this particular quality formalization or its terminology.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal affine normalization of a full-dimensional box to the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(u_i>\ell_i\) for every \(i\), set \(D=\operatorname{diag}(u-\ell)\), and let \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\). The maps
\[y=D^{-1}(x-\ell),\qquad x=\ell+Dy\]
are mutually inverse affine bijections between \(B\) and \([0,1]^n\). For \(\widehat f:[0,1]^n\to\mathbb{R}\) defined by \(\widehat f(y)=f(\ell+Dy)\),
\[\inf_{x\in B}f(x)=\inf_{y\in[0,1]^n}\widehat f(y).\]
Moreover, \(x^*\in B\) minimizes \(f\) over \(B\) if and only if \(D^{-1}(x^*-\ell)\) minimizes \(\widehat f\) over \([0,1]^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive box widths define an affine bijection to the unit cube. Objective infima are equal in the two coordinate systems, and any attained minimizers correspond under the bijection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is affinely bijective to \([0,1]^n\), \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)=\inf_{y\in[0,1]^n}\widehat f(y)\), and attained minimizers correspond.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

children.title: Coordinate Transforms
children.top_down_role: Changes of coordinates affecting curvature or separability.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Transforms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible affine reparameterization of localized problems and their underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty convex set, let \(T(y)=Ay+b\) with nonsingular \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and set \(C=T^{-1}(B)\). For any \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\), define \(g:C\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(g=f\circ T\). Then \(T:C\to B\) is a bijection and
\[\inf_{x\in B}f(x)=\inf_{y\in C}g(y).\]
A point \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\) over \(B\) if and only if \(T^{-1}(x^*)\) minimizes \(g\) over \(C\). If \(q:B\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and satisfies \(q(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\), then \(\widetilde q=q\circ T\) is convex on \(C\) and satisfies \(\widetilde q(y)\le g(y)\) for every \(y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine change of coordinates preserves objective infima and corresponds attained minimizers. Composing a convex underestimator with the transformation preserves both convexity and valid underestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\), and any underestimator \(q:B\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)=\inf_{y\in C}(f\circ T)(y)\), attained minimizers correspond, and every convex underestimator \(q\) on \(B\) induces the convex underestimator \(q\circ T\) on \(C\).

children.title: Conditioning Effects
children.top_down_role: Numerical plus relaxation-strength consequences of transformed domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative transformation laws explaining how affine scaling changes numerical curvature conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T(y)=Ay+b\) with nonsingular \(A\), and suppose \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on \(B=T(C)\). For \(g=f\circ T\),
\[
abla g(y)=A^{\mathsf T}
abla f(T(y)),\qquad 
abla^2g(y)=A^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(T(y))A.\]
Hence coordinate scaling changes curvature magnitudes and spectral conditioning by congruence. For the Euclidean condition number, \(\kappa_2(
abla^2g)\le\kappa_2(A)^2\kappa_2(
abla^2f)\) whenever the Hessians are positive definite; a poorly conditioned transform can therefore worsen conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine scaling congruently transforms Hessians, so it can improve curvature balance but may worsen condition numbers by up to the square of the transform's condition number.
assumptions_latex: The condition-number assertion is restricted to positive-definite Hessians.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla^2(f\circ T)(y)=A^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(T(y))A\) and \(\kappa_2(
abla^2g(y))\le\kappa_2(A)^2\kappa_2(
abla^2f(T(y)))\).

notation.meaning: spectral condition number of a positive-definite matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gradient and Hessian transformation laws and the positive-definite condition-number bound are mathematically plausible and properly qualified, but no matrix-analysis source is supplied.

children.title: Box-Restriction Tightening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening behavior as coordinate boxes contract.

knowledge_statements.title: Box-Restriction Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening and pointwise consistency of convex envelopes on nested boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be continuous on a box \(B\), and denote its convex envelope on a subbox \(C\subseteq B\) by \(\operatorname{vex}_C f\). If \(C_2\subseteq C_1\subseteq B\), then
\[\operatorname{vex}_{C_1}f(x)\le \operatorname{vex}_{C_2}f(x)\le f(x)\qquad(x\in C_2).\]
Furthermore, for nested boxes \(C_k\downarrow\{\bar x\}\), continuity gives \(\operatorname{vex}_{C_k}f(\bar x)\to f(\bar x)\). Thus exact convex underestimation strengthens as localization contracts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a function to a smaller box raises its convex envelope, and the envelope value converges to the function value as nested boxes shrink to a point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_{C_1}f\le\operatorname{vex}_{C_2}f\le f\) on \(C_2\), with pointwise convergence under nested contraction.

notation.meaning: convex envelope of f over C
nested boxes whose intersection is the singleton containing x-bar

children.title: Vertex-Facet Localization Geometry
children.top_down_role: Vertex- and facet-based regional geometry for affine and envelope models.

children.title: Simplex Interpolation Models
children.top_down_role: Vertex-interpolating models supported by simplicial geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Interpolation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique affine vertex interpolant on a nondegenerate simplex and its convexity-dependent bounding direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nondegenerate simplex. Every \(x\in S\) has unique barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_i(x)\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)=1\) and \(x=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)v_i\). The unique affine vertex interpolant of \(f\) is
\[I_Sf(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)f(v_i).\]
If \(f\) is convex on \(S\), then \(f(x)\le I_Sf(x)\); if \(f\) is concave, the inequality reverses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Barycentric coordinates define the unique affine interpolant through simplex vertices; it overestimates convex functions and underestimates concave functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_Sf(v_i)=f(v_i)\), with \(f\le I_Sf\) for convex \(f\) and \(I_Sf\le f\) for concave \(f\).

notation.meaning: affine vertex interpolant of f on S

children.title: Polyhedral Dual-Description Models
children.top_down_role: Lower models exploiting alternative polyhedral descriptions.

children.title: Polyhedral Vertex Models
children.top_down_role: Lower models constructed from extreme-point descriptions of polyhedral domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Vertex Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite vertex-ray representation of a polyhedron, specialized to vertices for bounded polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite point and direction sets \(V=\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}\) and \(R=\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\) in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), a vertex-ray model is
\[P=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_jv^j+\sum_{k=1}^q\mu_kr^k:\lambda\ge0,\ \mu\ge0,\ \sum_{j=1}^p\lambda_j=1\right\}.\]
It represents the Minkowski sum \(\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\). If \(P\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron, its recession cone is \(\{0\}\), so \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)\) for a finite vertex set \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron can be modeled by convex combinations of finitely many points plus conic combinations of recession directions; bounded polytopes require vertices only.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a nonempty finite subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\), and boundedness permits \(R=\varnothing\).

children.title: Polyhedral Facet Models
children.top_down_role: Lower models constructed from inequality descriptions of polyhedral domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Facet Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-space representation of polyhedra and irredundant facet inequalities for full-dimensional cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), the facet-form model
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\}\]
represents a closed convex polyhedron as a finite intersection of closed half-spaces. If \(P\) is full-dimensional and the description is irredundant, each inequality whose equality set meets \(P\) in dimension \(n-1\) defines a facet; redundant inequalities may be deleted without changing \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain:
A polyhedron is a finite intersection of half-spaces; in a full-dimensional irredundant description, dimension-
one boundary equalities define its facets.
assumptions_latex: The facet characterization assumes \(P\) is full-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\}\), with irredundant codimension-one active faces as facets.

children.title: Description-Sensitive Strength
children.top_down_role: Strength differences attributable to the selected polyhedral description.

knowledge_statements.title: Description-Sensitive Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact vertex and facet descriptions agree, while incomplete descriptions can induce distinct inner and outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope with exact descriptions \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\). If \(V'\subseteq V\) is nonempty, then
\[\operatorname{conv}(V')\subseteq P.\]
If some rows are deleted from \(Ax\le b\) and the remaining system defines \(P'\), then
\[P\subseteq P'.\]
Either inclusion can be strict, although redundancy can make it an equality. Consequently, for any objective \(h:P'\to\mathbb{R}\),
\[\inf_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(V')}h(x)\ge \inf_{x\in P}h(x)\ge \inf_{x\in P'}h(x).\]
Thus incomplete vertex and inequality descriptions can change approximation strength in opposite directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete vertex and inequality descriptions represent the same polytope. Retaining only some vertices gives an inner approximation, whereas deleting inequalities gives an outer approximation; either change may be strict and their minimization values move in opposite directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(V')\subseteq P\subseteq P'\) and \(\inf_{\operatorname{conv}(V')}h\ge\inf_Ph\ge\inf_{P'}h\).

notation.meaning: retained nonempty subset of generating vertices
objective compared across the three sets

children.title: Regular Subdivision Regimes
children.top_down_role: Refinement structures supporting consistent regional approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Subdivision Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coherent polyhedral subdivisions induced by lifting vertex data and projecting lower faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and assign heights \(h_j\in\mathbb{R}\). Form the lifted polytope \(Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(v^j,h_j):j=1,
\ldots,p\}\). The projections to \(\mathbb{R}^n\) of the lower faces of \(Q\) form a regular subdivision of \(\operatorname{conv}(V)\). Its cells cover \(\operatorname{conv}(V)\), and any two cells intersect in a common face. Refining the lower-face complex yields compatible regional polyhedral models without gaps or conflicting interiors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular subdivision is obtained by lifting vertices, taking lower faces, and projecting them; its cells cover the polytope and meet face-to-face.
assumptions_latex: Each point \(v^j\) has a finite lifting height \(h_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected lower faces constitute a face-to-face polyhedral subdivision of \(\operatorname{conv}(V)\).

notation.meaning: lifting height assigned to vertex j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifting construction is a standard definition of a regular subdivision and fits the topic, but no authoritative source is supplied for the lower-face projection, face-to-face property, or refinement assertion.

children.title: General Convex Localization
children.top_down_role: Lower bounding over nonbox convex regions and tractable containing sets.

children.title: Convex Outer Domains
children.top_down_role: Tractable convex regions containing the domain of interest.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Outer Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a convex localization region containing the nonconvex domain of interest.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(F\subseteq D\) be nonempty. A convex outer domain for \(D\) is a nonempty convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(D\subseteq C\). A function \(g:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is a valid convex underestimator relative to \(D\) when \(g\) is convex on \(C\) and \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Consequently, for every nonempty set \(R\) satisfying \(F\subseteq R\subseteq C\), \[\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex outer domain contains the domain of interest. A convex function lying below the objective on that domain gives a valid lower bound when minimized over any outer relaxation containing the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq C\), where \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) whenever \(F\subseteq R\subseteq C\).

notation.meaning: objective function on the domain of interest
convex underestimator on the outer domain

children.title: Bounding-Domain Modification Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Strength and tractability effects of enlarging or restricting the bounding domain.

children.title: Domain Extension
children.top_down_role: Use of enlarged bounding domains to obtain tractable lower models.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the validity and possible weakening caused by extending an underestimation domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty convex sets, let \(f:E\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(g:E\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex with \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in E\). Then \(g|_D\) is a convex underestimator of \(f|_D\), and \[\inf_{x\in E}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in D}f(x).\] Thus extension preserves validity on the original domain but can decrease the lower bound obtained by minimizing the underestimator over the extended domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An underestimator valid on a larger convex domain remains valid and convex on the original convex domain, but minimizing it over the larger domain can weaken the lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(g:E\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and satisfies \(g\leq f\) on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g|_D\leq f|_D\) and \(\inf_{x\in E}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: convex underestimator on the extended domain

source_refs.locator: 2.6.2 Lipschitzian Extension of the Objective Function p. 120

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6.2 Lipschitzian Extension of the Objective Function p. 120

children.title: Domain Restriction
children.top_down_role: Use of smaller valid regions to strengthen lower models.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States how localization to a smaller domain strengthens a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D'\subseteq D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty convex sets, let \(F\subseteq D'\) be nonempty, and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\). Suppose \(g:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and satisfies \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Then \(g|_{D'}\) is convex and remains valid for the same feasible problem, and \[\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in D'}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] Hence restricting the relaxation domain while retaining every feasible point cannot worsen the lower bound produced by the same underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a convex relaxation to a smaller convex set that still contains every feasible point preserves validity and cannot decrease the lower bound from the same underestimator.
assumptions_latex: \(g:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and satisfies \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in D'}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: objective function on the feasible set

children.title: Strength–Tractability Effects
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs induced by enlarging or restricting the bounding domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Tractability Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the monotone strength effect of localization from representation-dependent tractability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1\subseteq D_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty convex sets, and let \(f:D_2\to\mathbb{R}\). For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), suppose the pointwise greatest real-valued convex underestimator \(v_i\) of \(f|_{D_i}\) exists. Every convex underestimator on \(D_2\) restricts to a convex underestimator on \(D_1\), so \(v_1(x)\geq v_2(x)\) for every \(x\in D_1\). This ordering concerns relaxation strength; computational tractability additionally depends on the representations of \(D_i\) and \(v_i\) and on the optimization method used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On nested convex localization domains, the envelope on the smaller domain is at least as strong pointwise. Computational tractability also depends on representation and solution method, not only on set inclusion.
assumptions_latex: The greatest real-valued convex underestimators \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_1(x)\geq v_2(x)\) for every \(x\in D_1\); this does not by itself determine computational tractability.

notation.meaning: objective function on the larger domain

children.title: Coordinate-Free Local Models
children.top_down_role: Regional models based on norms, support geometry, or non-axis-aligned curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Free Local Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a basis-independent quadratic convex underestimator from a curvature lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space, let \(f\) be twice differentiable on an open set containing \(C\), and let \(Q\) be a positive-semidefinite self-adjoint operator such that \(\nabla^2 f(y)-Q\) is positive semidefinite for every \(y\in C\). For any \(x_0\in C\), the model \[m_{x_0}(x)=f(x_0)+\langle\nabla f(x_0),x-x_0\rangle+\tfrac12\langle x-x_0,Q(x-x_0)\rangle\] is convex and satisfies \(m_{x_0}(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite curvature lower operator produces a convex quadratic underestimator expressed intrinsically through inner products, without coordinate-aligned boxes.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(f\) is twice differentiable near \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_{x_0}\) is convex on \(C\) and \(m_{x_0}(x)\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\in C\).

children.title: Constraint-Aware Localization
children.top_down_role: Use of feasible-set and constraint information to strengthen objective and constraint relaxations.

children.title: Feasible-Set-Restricted Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope objects formed relative to the actual feasible region.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Set-Restricted Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the convex envelope using domination only on the actual feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\). Define \[\mathcal{G}_F=\{g:\operatorname{conv}(F)\to\mathbb{R}:g\text{ is convex and }g(y)\leq f(y)\text{ for every }y\in F\}.\] The feasible-set-restricted convex envelope is the pointwise supremum \[\operatorname{vex}_F f(x)=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{G}_F}g(x),\qquad x\in\operatorname{conv}(F).\] If \(\mathcal{G}_F\) is nonempty and this supremum is finite for every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(F)\), then \(\operatorname{vex}_F f\) is the greatest real-valued convex function on \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\) satisfying \(\operatorname{vex}_F f(y)\leq f(y)\) for every \(y\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible-set-restricted convex envelope is the pointwise supremum of convex functions on the convex hull that are dominated by the objective at feasible points. When the admissible family is nonempty and the supremum is finite everywhere, it is the greatest such real-valued convex function.
assumptions_latex: For the real-valued greatest-function conclusion, \(\mathcal{G}_F\neq\varnothing\) and the pointwise supremum is finite on \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_F f(x)=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{G}_F}g(x)\), and under the stated existence conditions it is the greatest real-valued convex function dominated by \(f\) on \(F\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of the feasible set
family of real-valued convex functions dominated by f on F

children.title: Constraint-Propagated Ranges
children.top_down_role: Variable and intermediate ranges tightened using constraint information.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Propagated Ranges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exact variable ranges implied jointly by the current constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(c_j:D\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \[C=\{x\in D:c_j(x)\leq0\text{ for every }j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\}\] be nonempty. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), suppose the quantities \[\ell_i^*=\inf_{x\in C}x_i,\qquad u_i^*=\sup_{x\in C}x_i\] are finite. Every \(x\in C\) satisfies \(\ell_i^*\leq x_i\leq u_i^*\), and every interval \([\ell_i,u_i]\) containing all feasible values of coordinate \(i\) satisfies \(\ell_i\leq\ell_i^*\) and \(u_i^*\leq u_i\). Thus a propagated interval is valid only if it remains an outer enclosure of \([\ell_i^*,u_i^*]\); it is a valid tightening of a current interval when it is also contained in that current interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing a coordinate over the constrained set gives its tightest feasible range. Constraint propagation may replace a current interval by a smaller outer interval only when the new interval still contains every feasible coordinate value.
assumptions_latex: The constraint-defined feasible set \(C\) is nonempty.
For each considered coordinate, \(\ell_i^*\) and \(u_i^*\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C\Rightarrow \ell_i^*\leq x_i\leq u_i^*\), and every valid containing interval includes \([\ell_i^*,u_i^*]\).

notation.meaning: exact feasible lower and upper bounds for coordinate i

children.title: Joint Objective–Constraint Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexification exploiting relationships among multiple model components.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Objective–Constraint Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the strongest joint convex relaxation as a convex hull in shared lifted space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), with objective \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) and constraints \(c_j:D\to\mathbb{R}\). Define the joint lifted set \[S=\{(x,t,z)\in D\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^m:t\geq f(x),\ z_j\geq c_j(x),\ j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Its closed convex hull \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(S)\) is the smallest closed convex set containing every simultaneous objective–constraint epigraph tuple. Imposing \((x,t,z)\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(S)\) together with \(z\leq0\) therefore gives a valid joint convex relaxation of minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c_j(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying the shared lifted objective–constraint set preserves relationships among all components and yields a valid joint relaxation after enforcing nonpositive constraint epigraph variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,f(x),c(x))\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(S)\), and \(z\leq0\) yields a valid convex relaxation of the original inequalities.

children.title: Valid Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Certification routes by which relaxations and enclosures support rigorous lower bounds.

children.title: Relaxation-Derived Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds inherited from relaxed objectives and outer-approximated feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Derived Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies a lower bound from an outer feasible relaxation and objective underestimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F\subseteq R\), and let \(g:R\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). If a scalar \(L\) is certified to satisfy \(L\leq\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\), then \[L\leq\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}g(x)\leq p^*.\] The data \((R,g,L)\), together with checks of containment, underestimation, and the relaxed optimum bound, constitute a lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer feasible set, an objective underestimator, and a certified bound on the relaxed minimum together certify a lower bound for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

children.title: Dual-Derived Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds inherited from weak-duality and convex-dual mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Derived Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the weak-duality certificate for a constrained minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X	o\mathbb{R}\), let \(h:X	o\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p	imes n}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\). Define \[p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ h_i(x)\leq0	ext{ for }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\ Ax=b\}.\] For \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) and \(
u\in\mathbb{R}^p\), define \[q(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X} igl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+
u^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b) igr).\] Weak duality gives \(q(\lambda,
u)\leq p^*\). Therefore any certified scalar \(L\) satisfying \(L\leq q(\lambda,
u)\) is a lower-bound certificate: \[L\leq q(\lambda,
u)\leq p^*.\] Strong duality is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a specified constrained minimization problem, nonnegative inequality multipliers and arbitrary equality multipliers define a Lagrangian dual value below the primal optimum. Any certified lower bound on that dual value is therefore a valid lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq q(\lambda,\nu)\leq p^*\).

children.title: Enclosure-Derived Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds inherited from rigorous range and curvature enclosures.

knowledge_statements.title: Enclosure-Derived Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies a lower bound using rigorous value or curvature enclosures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A value enclosure certifies \(f(x)\in[\underline f(D),\overline f(D)]\) for every \(x\in D\), immediately giving \(\underline f(D)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). More generally, suppose certified derivative or curvature enclosures construct a function \(g:D\to\mathbb{R}\) with \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) throughout \(D\). If \(L\leq\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\) is also rigorously enclosed, then \[L\leq\inf_{x\in D}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] The verified enclosures and their domain form the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorous range lower endpoint, or a rigorously constructed underestimator with an enclosed minimum, certifies a lower bound over every feasible subset.
assumptions_latex: All stated value, derivative, or curvature enclosures hold for every point of \(D\).
\(L\leq\inf_D g\) when an underestimator is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline f(D)\leq\inf_F f\), or respectively \(L\leq\inf_F f\).

notation.meaning: rigorous range enclosure of the objective on \(D\)
rigorous lower bound on the underestimator minimum

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract lower-bound implications are mathematically sound and certificate is the appropriate content kind, but no citation supports the rigorous value, derivative, or curvature enclosure conventions.

children.title: Machine-Certified Bounds
children.top_down_role: Numerically rigorous bounds accounting for rounding and optimization tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Machine-Certified Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a numerically rigorous lower-bound certificate robust to rounding and solver tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), let a machine-checkable certificate specify an outer set \(R\supseteq F\), an underestimator \(g\), and a scalar \(L\). Directed-rounding or exact-arithmetic verification must establish \(g(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(L\leq\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\), including all optimization residuals and tolerances. These verified inclusions imply \[L\leq\inf_{x\in R}g(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=p^*.\] A floating-point solver value without such error accounting is not, by itself, a valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A machine-certified lower bound requires rigorous containment, underestimation, and relaxed-optimum checks that explicitly account for rounding, residuals, and solver tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(g\leq f\) on \(F\) is verified with rigorous arithmetic.
\(L\leq\inf_R g\) includes rounding and optimization error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\leq p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated implication is correct and belongs in a certificate leaf, but the claims about directed rounding, residual accounting, and machine-checkability require an authoritative verified-numerics or solver-certificate source.

children.title: Regional Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower bounds attached to restricted domains, subproblems, and partition regions.

children.title: Subproblem Bound Objects
children.top_down_role: Bounds associated with individual restricted optimization regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Bound Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional lower-bound object for a restricted minimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_R=F\cap R\) be a nonempty regional feasible set and let \(v_R=\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\). A subproblem lower-bound object is a tuple \(B_R=(R,Q_R,\phi_R,\ell_R)\), where \(F_R\subseteq Q_R\), \(\phi_R(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_R\), and \(\ell_R=\inf_{x\in Q_R}\phi_R(x)\) is finite. Consequently, \(\ell_R\leq v_R\). The tuple records the region, its relaxation, its underestimating objective, and the certified regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional bound object packages a region, a relaxation, an underestimator, and its optimum; that optimum cannot exceed the true regional optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_R=\inf_{x\in Q_R}\phi_R(x)\leq v_R\)

notation.meaning: feasible set restricted to region R
relaxation of the regional feasible set

children.title: Restriction Monotonicity
children.top_down_role: Validity and strengthening relationships under domain restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of exact and consistently constructed relaxation bounds under region restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq R\), so that \(F_S\subseteq F_R\). Then the exact regional optima satisfy \(v_S=\inf_{x\in F_S}f(x)\geq\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)=v_R\). Suppose additionally that the relaxation construction is restriction-consistent: \(Q_S\subseteq Q_R\) and \(\phi_S(x)\geq\phi_R(x)\) for every \(x\in Q_S\). For \(\ell_T=\inf_{x\in Q_T}\phi_T(x)\), these conditions imply \(\ell_S\geq\ell_R\). Domain restriction alone does not imply monotonicity for independently chosen relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a region raises its exact minimum. Its relaxation bound also rises when the child relaxation and underestimator are constructed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_S\geq v_R\quad\text{and}\quad\ell_S\geq\ell_R\)

notation.meaning: relaxation lower bound for region T

children.title: Partition-Tree Bound Relations
children.top_down_role: Parent, child, and sibling relationships among regional bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Tree Bound Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid parent bounds obtained from lower bounds on covering child regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a parent region \(R\) have children \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) satisfying \(F_R=\bigcup_{i=1}^m F_{R_i}\). If \(\ell_i\leq\inf_{x\in F_{R_i}}f(x)\) for every child, then \(\min_{1\leq i\leq m}\ell_i\leq\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\). If \(\ell_R\) is an independently valid parent bound, the strengthened parent bound is \(\widehat\ell_R=\max\{\ell_R,\min_i\ell_i\}\). No ordering between sibling bounds follows merely from their being siblings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum child bound is valid for a covered parent; taking its maximum with an existing parent bound strengthens the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\ell_R=\max\{\ell_R,\min_i\ell_i\}\leq\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\)

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for child i

children.title: Root-Relaxation Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower-bound certificate obtained before partitioning the original domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the feasible set of the global problem with value \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). If the root relaxation has feasible set \(Q_0\supseteq F\) and objective \(\phi_0\) satisfying \(\phi_0(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\), then \(L_0=\inf_{x\in Q_0}\phi_0(x)\) is a global lower-bound certificate. In particular, \(L_0\leq p^*\), regardless of whether the relaxation optimizer is feasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing an underestimator over a superset of the full feasible domain produces a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_0=\inf_{x\in Q_0}\phi_0(x)\leq p^*\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) with \(m\geq1\), let \(\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) be active regions whose restricted feasible sets cover the global feasible set: \(F=\bigcup_{i=1}^m(F\cap R_i)\). For every \(i\in\mathcal A\), let \(\ell_i\leq\inf_{x\in F\cap R_i}f(x)\). Then the aggregate \(L_{\mathcal A}=\min_{i\in\mathcal A}\ell_i\) satisfies \(L_{\mathcal A}\leq p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Removing a region preserves this certificate only when the remaining regions still cover the global feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty finite active cover, the minimum of the valid regional lower bounds is a valid global lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a possibly nonconvex constrained minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\leq0,\ h(x)=0\}\). For multipliers \(\lambda\geq0\) and unrestricted \(
u\), define \(q(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X} igl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)+
u^{\mathsf T}h(x) igr)\). Every such dual value satisfies \(q(\lambda,
u)\leq p^*\). Hence the dual optimum \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0,
u}q(\lambda,
u)\) is also a global lower bound whenever it is well-defined; convexity and strong duality are unnecessary for validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible Lagrange multiplier pair yields a global lower bound by weak duality, even for a nonconvex primal problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda,\nu)\leq d^*\leq p^*\)

children.title: Hybrid Global Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination rule for independently valid relaxation, dual, and enclosure bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_1,\ldots,L_k\) be finite lower bounds for the same global minimization problem, so that \(L_j\leq p^*\) for every \(j\). The hybrid bound \(L_{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max_{1\leq j\leq k}L_j\) is valid and dominates every constituent bound: \(L_j\leq L_{\mathrm{hyb}}\leq p^*\). The constituents may arise from primal relaxations, dual certificates, interval enclosures, or other validated mechanisms, provided they use the same objective scale and problem definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of compatible valid global lower bounds is itself valid and at least as strong as every constituent bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_j\leq L_{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max_jL_j\leq p^*\)

children.title: Gap Normalizations

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{abs}},g_{\mathrm{rel}},g_{\mathrm{sc}}\geq0\), and \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=0\Longleftrightarrow g_{\mathrm{rel}}=0\Longleftrightarrow g_{\mathrm{sc}}=0\Longleftrightarrow U=L\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute, relative, and symmetric scale-aware conventions for a certified optimality gap.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite bounds \(L\leq p^*\leq U\) and a safeguard \(\varepsilon>0\), define the absolute gap by \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\), the incumbent-relative gap by \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/\max\{\varepsilon,|U|\}\), and the symmetric scale-aware gap by \(g_{\mathrm{sc}}=(U-L)/\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\). All three gaps are nonnegative, and each vanishes exactly when \(U=L\). A reported normalized gap must identify its denominator convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute gaps use the bound difference; relative and scale-aware gaps divide it by an explicitly declared positive scale. Each defined gap is nonnegative and is zero exactly when the bounds coincide.

children.title: Regional Gaps
children.top_down_role: Relaxation gaps attached to individual localized regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified gap between regional feasible and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a region \(R\), let \(v_R=\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\), let \(\ell_R\leq v_R\) be a finite certified lower bound, and let \(u_R=f(\bar x_R)\geq v_R\) for some \(\bar x_R\in F\cap R\). The regional absolute gap is \(g_R=u_R-\ell_R\geq0\). If \(g_R=0\), then \(u_R=\ell_R=v_R\), so \(\bar x_R\) is globally optimal within \(R\). A normalized regional gap is obtained by applying a declared positive scaling denominator to \(g_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional gap is the difference between a feasible regional objective value and a certified regional lower bound; zero certifies regional optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_R=u_R-\ell_R\geq0\), and \(g_R=0\Longrightarrow u_R=v_R=\ell_R\)

notation.meaning: regional lower and feasible upper bounds

children.title: Global Gaps
children.top_down_role: Relaxation gaps attached to the complete search representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality certificate formed from a feasible incumbent and global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), let \(L\leq p^*\) be a certified global lower bound, and let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a feasible point \(\bar x\in F\). The global absolute gap is \(G=U-L\geq0\), and it bounds incumbent suboptimality by \(0\leq U-p^*\leq G\). Thus \(G\leq\tau\) certifies absolute \(\tau\)-optimality, while \(G=0\) certifies \(U=L=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global bound difference upper-bounds incumbent suboptimality; a gap below tolerance certifies approximate global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq U-p^*\leq G=U-L\)

notation.meaning: global lower bound and feasible incumbent value

children.title: Cross-Region Gap Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Relationships between regional gap information plus global gap assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Region Gap Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between global and regional gaps over a finite active cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let active regions cover \(F\), with finite regional lower bounds \(\ell_i\) and feasible regional values \(u_i\). Define \(L=\min_i\ell_i\) and \(U=\min_i u_i\). Then the global gap has the representation \(U-L=\max_i(U-\ell_i)\). Since \(U\leq u_i\) for every \(i\), it follows that \(U-L\leq\max_i(u_i-\ell_i)\). Equality with the maximum regional gap need not hold because the global incumbent and weakest lower bound may come from different regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global gap is the largest difference between the global incumbent and a regional lower bound, and is bounded by the largest regional gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L=\max_i(U-\ell_i)\leq\max_i(u_i-\ell_i)\)

children.title: Gap-Source Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Separation attributable to objective, constraint, formulation, and numerical relaxation effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Source Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-dependent telescoping attribution of bound weakness to declared relaxation stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a declared sequence of valid bounds \(L^{(0)}\leq L^{(1)}\leq L^{(2)}\leq L^{(3)}\leq L^{(4)}\leq U\), where successive stages repair, in a fixed order, objective, constraint, formulation, and numerical relaxation effects. Define \(\delta_s=L^{(s)}-L^{(s-1)}\geq0\) for \(s=1,\ldots,4\) and \(r=U-L^{(4)}\geq0\). Then \(U-L^{(0)}=r+\sum_{s=1}^4\delta_s\). The component values are conditional on the selected intermediate bounds and ordering; without these choices, no unique additive source decomposition exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gap can be telescoped across staged bound improvements, but the attributed components depend on the chosen stages and their order.
assumptions_latex: Each stage changes one declared relaxation source.

notation.meaning: gap reduction attributed to stage s
residual gap after all declared stages

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping identity is algebraically valid, and the record appropriately warns that the decomposition depends on the selected stages and ordering. However, no source is supplied for interpreting the four increments specifically as objective, constraint, formulation, and numerical relaxation effects, so the named gap-source decomposition cannot yet be accepted.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\neq\varnothing\) be a feasible set, let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and define \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). A pair \((\hat x,L)\) is an exact global-optimality certificate if \(\hat x\in F\), \(L\le f^*\), and \(f(\hat x)=L\). Its certified conclusion is \(f(\hat x)=f^*=L\) and \(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\). The lower-bound assertion must be justified by a valid relaxation, dual certificate, or exhaustive bound argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and a rigorously justified global lower bound form an exact certificate when the point's objective value equals that bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and define the finite value \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a feasible point \(\hat x\in F\) and a certified lower bound \(L\le f^*\) form an \(\varepsilon\)-global-optimality certificate if \(f(\hat x)-L\le\varepsilon\). The certified conclusion is \(0\le f(\hat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\). This is an absolute-gap certificate; a relative-gap certificate requires a separately specified scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent is certified globally epsilon-optimal when its gap above a valid global lower bound is at most epsilon.

children.title: Regional Exclusion Certificates
children.top_down_role: Bound- and infeasibility-based certificates excluding restricted regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Regional Exclusion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion of a region by infeasibility or an incumbent-dominating lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f\) over \(F\), and let \(R\) be a restricted region. The region has an infeasibility exclusion certificate if it proves \(F\cap R=\varnothing\). Given an incumbent \(\hat x\in F\) with \(U=f(\hat x)\), it has a bound exclusion certificate if a valid regional bound \(L_R\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\) satisfies \(L_R>U\). In either case, \(R\) contains no global minimizer improving upon the incumbent; under the strict bound inequality, it contains no global minimizer at all.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region can be discarded when it is infeasible or its valid lower bound exceeds a feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap R=\varnothing\) or \(L_R>U\) implies \(R\cap\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound over the region

children.title: Pointwise Underestimator Dominance

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Underestimator Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering of two underestimators on the same domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(u_1,u_2:D\to\mathbb R\) be valid underestimators. If \[u_1(x)\le u_2(x)\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in D,\] then \(u_2\) pointwise dominates \(u_1\). Their minimization bounds satisfy \[\inf_{x\in D}u_1(x)\le\inf_{x\in D}u_2(x)\le\inf_{x\in D}f(x).\] Hence replacing \(u_1\) by \(u_2\) cannot weaken the global lower bound, although equality of the two infima may occur despite strict pointwise improvement elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise larger valid underestimator is at least as strong because its minimum gives no smaller lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_D u_1\le\inf_D u_2\le\inf_D f\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Relaxation-Set Inclusion
children.top_down_role: Comparison through containment of convex relaxed feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Set Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength ordering for minimization relaxations by feasible-set containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\subseteq X\), where \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are relaxed feasible sets for minimizing an objective \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). Then \(R_1\) is at least as strong as \(R_2\), and their optimal values obey \[\inf_{x\in R_2}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in R_1}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] Thus the smaller relaxation produces a lower bound no worse than that of the larger relaxation. This ordering concerns bound strength, not the computational cost of optimizing over either set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, a relaxation contained in another valid relaxation yields an equal or higher lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{R_2}f\le\inf_{R_1}f\le\inf_F f\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Extended-Formulation Projection Strength
children.top_down_role: Comparison of lifted relaxations after projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Projection Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison of lifted relaxations in the original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the original feasible set and let \(Q_i\subseteq X\times Y_i\) be lifted relaxations satisfying \(F\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_i)\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\). If \[\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_X(Q_2),\] then \(Q_1\) is projection-stronger than \(Q_2\). For every objective \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) depending only on the original variables, \[\inf_{(x,y_2)\in Q_2}f(x)\le\inf_{(x,y_1)\in Q_1}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] Auxiliary-space inclusion is unnecessary; only projected containment determines this strength ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted relaxation is stronger when its projection onto the original variables is contained in the competing projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{Q_2}f(x)\le\inf_{Q_1}f(x)\le\inf_F f(x)\).

notation.meaning: lifted relaxation in original and auxiliary variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-based strength statement is mathematically plausible and the property content kind fits the leaf, but the record has no citation. An authoritative source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required for the lifted-formulation claim.

children.title: Refinement Consistency
children.top_down_role: Convergence of regional relaxations as localization regions contract or formulations are refined.

children.title: Pointwise Relaxation Convergence
children.top_down_role: Closing of pointwise relaxation error under refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Relaxation Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise closing of underestimation error along a refinement sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \((u_k)_{k\ge1}\) be valid underestimators satisfying \(u_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). The relaxations converge pointwise to \(f\) if \[\lim_{k\to\infty}u_k(x)=f(x)\qquad\text{for every fixed }x\in D.\] Equivalently, the pointwise relaxation error \(e_k(x)=f(x)-u_k(x)\) tends to zero for each fixed \(x\). This definition imposes no uniform rate and does not by itself imply convergence of minimizing points or optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise convergence means that the underestimation error vanishes at every fixed point as refinement proceeds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\to f\) pointwise exactly when \(f(x)-u_k(x)\to0\) for every \(x\in D\).

source_refs.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

source_witnesses.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

children.title: Functional-Epigraphical Convergence Pair
children.top_down_role: Setwise and uniform convergence regimes for functions and epigraphs.

children.title: Uniform Convergence
children.top_down_role: Uniform approximation behavior of underestimators over specified domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform closing of relaxation error over a common domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(u_k:D\to\mathbb R\). The sequence \((u_k)\) converges uniformly to \(f\) on \(D\) if \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\sup_{x\in D}|u_k(x)-f(x)|=0.\] If every \(u_k\) is an underestimator of \(f\), the absolute value may be replaced by the nonnegative error \(f(x)-u_k(x)\). Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), one index \(K\) works simultaneously for all \(x\in D\) and all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convergence requires one refinement threshold to make the relaxation error small simultaneously throughout the domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\to f\) uniformly if and only if \(\sup_{x\in D}|u_k(x)-f(x)|\to0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform-convergence definition is precise and correctly adapted to one-sided underestimation error, but no source is supplied. A specific authoritative functional-analysis locator is required.

children.title: Epigraphical Convergence
children.top_down_role: Setwise convergence behavior of relaxation epigraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraphical Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential characterization of epi-convergence on a metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a metric space and let \(f_k,f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). The sequence \((f_k)\) epi-converges to \(f\) if, for every \(x\in X\), both conditions hold: for every sequence \(x_k\to x\), \[f(x)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}f_k(x_k),\] and there exists a recovery sequence \(x_k\to x\) such that \[f(x)\ge\limsup_{k\to\infty}f_k(x_k).\] Equivalently in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the epigraphs converge to \(\operatorname{epi}f\) in the Painlevé–Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epi-convergence combines a universal lower-limit inequality with a recovery sequence attaining the matching upper limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_k\xrightarrow{\mathrm{epi}}f\) exactly when the liminf and recovery-sequence conditions hold at every \(x\in X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential liminf and recovery-sequence conditions are the standard metric-space formulation, and definition is the correct content kind. No source supports either the definition or the stated finite-dimensional Painleve-Kuratowski equivalence, so an authoritative variational-analysis locator is required.

children.title: Convergence-Mode Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Implications plus distinctions among function-level or setwise convergence modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence-Mode Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implications and strict separations among uniform, pointwise, and epi-convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real-valued functions \(f_k,f\) on a metric space, uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence. If \(f\) is lower semicontinuous, uniform convergence also implies epi-convergence. Neither converse holds generally. On \([-1,1]\), the continuous functions \(f_k(x)=\max\{0,1-k|x|\}\) epi-converge to the zero function, but fail to converge pointwise at \(x=0\). Conversely, functions with \(g_k(1/k)=-1\) and \(g_k(x)=0\) otherwise converge pointwise to zero, but do not epi-converge to zero because the sequence \(x_k=1/k\to0\) violates the epi-liminf inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convergence implies pointwise and, for a lower-semicontinuous limit, epi-convergence; explicit moving-spike examples separate the converses.
assumptions_latex: \(f_k,f\) are real-valued on a metric space.
\(f\) is lower semicontinuous for the uniform-to-epi implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_k\to f\) uniformly implies pointwise convergence and epi-convergence, while the displayed examples disprove both converses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated implications and moving-spike separations are mathematically coherent, and failure_boundary is appropriate because the record emphasizes failed converses. The record nevertheless lacks citations for both the uniform-to-epi implication and the counterexamples.

children.title: Relaxation Convergence Orders
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic quality families for primitive, factorable, interval-assisted, and curvature relaxations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Najman and Mitsos, Convergence Rate of McCormick Relaxations
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Najman and Mitsos, Convergence Rate of McCormick Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Convergence Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case asymptotic order of underestimation error under refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(u_h:D\to\mathbb R\) be valid underestimators indexed by a refinement scale \(h>0\). Define \(E(h)=\sup_{x\in D}(f(x)-u_h(x))\). The relaxation has uniform convergence order at least \(p>0\) if there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(h_0>0\) such that \[E(h)\le C h^p\qquad\text{for all }0<h\le h_0.\] It has exact order \(p\) when additionally \(E(h)\ge c h^p\) for some \(c>0\) and all sufficiently small \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convergence order is the power of the refinement scale governing the worst-case relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(h)=O(h^p)\) defines order at least \(p\), while \(E(h)=\Theta(h^p)\) defines exact order \(p\).

source_refs.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282
