children.title: Decoupled-Constraint Weakness
children.top_down_role: Loss of joint structure when related components are relaxed independently.

knowledge_statements.title: Decoupled-Constraint Weakness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent relaxation of constraints sharing a variable can erase equality implied by their joint structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x,y_1,y_2\in[0,1]\) subject to \(y_1=x\), \(y_2=x\), and \(y_1+y_2=1\). The joint system has the unique solution \(x=y_1=y_2=1/2\). If the two defining constraints are relaxed with independent copies \(x_1,x_2\in[0,1]\), imposing only \(y_1=x_1\), \(y_2=x_2\), and \(y_1+y_2=1\), then every \((y_1,y_2)=(t,1-t)\) with \(t\in[0,1]\) is feasible. Decoupling therefore strictly enlarges the projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a shared variable into independent copies turns a unique jointly feasible point into an entire line segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(y_1,y_2)\}=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\) jointly, but the decoupled projection is \(\{(t,1-t):0\leq t\leq1\}\).

notation.meaning: independent copies replacing the original shared variable x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact feasible-set elimination directly establishes the strict enlargement
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint system and decoupled projection are correctly characterized, and counterexample fits the exact terminal topic. No authoritative source reference with a specific locator is supplied, so the record remains needs_source.

children.title: Certification Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent failure of valid lower models to improve certification progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Certification Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent local relaxation error prevents branch-and-bound certification despite continued node processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of a continuous function on a compact set. At iteration \(k\), let \(U_k\) be the incumbent value, let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the active regions, and let \(L(R)\) be a valid lower bound on region \(R\). Define \(L_k=\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}L(R)\). If an infinite active chain \((R_k)\) contains a global minimizer \(x^*\), is never fathomed, and satisfies \(L(R_k)\le f(x^*)-\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), then \(L_k\le f(x^*)-\delta\). Consequently, whenever \(U_k\ge f(x^*)\), the absolute certification gap obeys \(U_k-L_k\ge\delta\), so no tolerance \(\varepsilon<\delta\) can be certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a surviving region containing a global minimizer retains a fixed positive lower-bound error, the global optimality gap cannot fall below that error.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous and the feasible set is compact.
An infinite active chain containing \(x^*\) has relaxation error at least \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k\ge\delta\), hence certification with \(\varepsilon<\delta\) is impossible.

notation.meaning: incumbent feasible objective value at iteration k
smallest lower bound among active regions

children.title: Weakness-to-Stagnation Transitions
children.top_down_role: Regimes where relaxation gaps translate into stalled bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakness-to-Stagnation Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes transient relaxation weakness from error that survives refinement along an active branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) be continuous on a nonempty compact feasible set \(F\), let \(x^*\in F\) satisfy \(f(x^*)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\), and consider a branch-and-bound procedure. At iteration \(k\), let \(U_k\) be an incumbent feasible value, let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the active regions, and define \(L_k=\min_{R\in\mathcal A_k}L(R)\), where \(L(R)\le\min_{x\in R\cap F}f(x)\) whenever \(R\cap F\ne\varnothing\). Let \(R_k\in\mathcal A_k\) form a nested chain with \(R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\) and \(x^*\in R_k\) for every \(k\), and define \(e(R_k)=\min_{x\in R_k\cap F}f(x)-L(R_k)\). Weakness is transient when \(e(R_k)\to0\). If instead \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}e(R_k)=\delta>0\) and \(U_k\to f(x^*)\), then \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}(U_k-L_k)\ge\delta\). Thus shrinking region diameter alone does not prevent certification stagnation unless the relaxation becomes asymptotically exact along the chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation weakness becomes certification stagnation when a positive lower-bound defect persists along an active refined branch containing an optimizer; even convergent incumbents then leave a positive limiting certification gap.
assumptions_latex: \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(F\) is nonempty and compact.
For each \(k\), \(R_k\in\mathcal A_k\), \(R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), and \(x^*\in R_k\cap F\).
\(L(R)\) is a valid lower bound on every relevant nonempty regional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}e(R_k)=\delta>0\), then \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}(U_k-L_k)\ge\delta\).

notation.meaning: nested active region containing a global minimizer at iteration k
incumbent feasible objective value at iteration k
smallest lower bound among active regions at iteration k

children.title: Representation Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Material differences among relaxations of equivalent mathematical expressions.

children.title: Expression-Graph Dependence
children.top_down_role: Strength variation caused by operation ordering and common-subexpression handling.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive convex relaxations need not be invariant under algebraically equivalent expression graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two directed acyclic expression graphs \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) represent the same function on a box \(X\), and let \(\mathcal R(G_i,X)\) be the lifted feasible set obtained by replacing each primitive operation with a chosen convex relaxation. Algebraic equivalence of the represented functions does not imply \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}\mathcal R(G_1,X)=\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}\mathcal R(G_2,X)\). In particular, if repeated occurrences of a common subexpression are assigned independent auxiliary variables without equality links, the resulting lifted set contains the set produced by sharing one auxiliary variable. Minimizing the terminal variable therefore gives a lower bound no stronger than that from the shared-subexpression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent formulas can yield different convex bounds; duplicating a common subexpression without equality links can only weaken the shared-node formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) compute the same function on \(X\).
Each primitive replacement is a valid convex relaxation over its declared bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent duplicated subexpressions yield a relaxation containing the corresponding shared-subexpression relaxation and hence a weakly smaller minimization bound.

children.title: Lift-Projection Relaxation Loss
children.top_down_role: Weakness introduced by auxiliary-variable decoupling or incomplete linking structure.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Decoupling
children.top_down_role: Relaxation weakness introduced when lifted variables lose essential dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Decoupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicated auxiliaries enlarge a relaxation when equality or consistency links are omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\times Y\) be a convex relaxation of the graph of \(h:X\to Y\). A shared lift uses one auxiliary \(y\) with \((x,y)\in C\). A decoupled lift replaces two uses of \(h(x)\) by \(y_1,y_2\) satisfying \((x,y_1)\in C\) and \((x,y_2)\in C\), but omits \(y_1=y_2\). The shared lift, embedded by \(y_1=y_2=y\), is contained in the decoupled lift. If some fiber \(C_x=\{y:(x,y)\in C\}\) contains distinct points, the containment is strict, and an objective or constraint involving both copies may obtain a strictly weaker relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting equality between duplicate auxiliary variables enlarges the lifted feasible set whenever the primitive relaxation has a non-singleton fiber.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a valid convex relaxation of \(\{(x,h(x)):x\in X\}\).
Two occurrences of \(h(x)\) are represented by separate auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decoupled lift contains the shared lift, strictly whenever \(C_x\) is non-singleton for some \(x\).

notation.meaning: fiber of the primitive relaxation at x

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

children.title: Incomplete Linking Structure
children.top_down_role: Gaps attributable to missing or insufficient connections among lifted variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Linking Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Missing valid cross-primitive constraints creates a strictly larger lifted relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be an exact lifted feasible set and let \(Q=\bigcap_{j=1}^q Q_j\) be the intersection of convex primitive relaxations, so \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\subseteq Q\). Suppose a valid linking inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le b\) holds on \(S\) but is omitted from \(Q\), and some \(\bar z\in Q\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar z>b\). Then \(Q\) strictly contains \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Moreover, for the linear objective \(-a^{\mathsf T}z\), minimization over \(Q\) gives a strictly smaller value than minimization over \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Thus local primitive validity does not compensate for missing global links.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an omitted linking inequality cuts off a relaxed point, the primitive-wise relaxation is strictly larger and is weaker for a separating linear objective.
assumptions_latex: Some \(\bar z\in Q\) violates the linking inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\supsetneq\operatorname{conv}(S)\), with a strictly weaker bound for objective \(-a^{\mathsf T}z\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical separation claim is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the generic model-structure locator does not inspectably support the asserted effect of an omitted linking inequality.

children.title: Projection-Induced Relaxation Loss
children.top_down_role: Underestimation weakness that appears after eliminating lifted coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Induced Relaxation Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection preserves an exact convex hull; loss arises from an inexact lifted outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\), let \(P\) denote projection onto the original variables, and let \(Q\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(S)\) be a convex lifted relaxation. Linear projection commutes with convexification, so \(P(\operatorname{conv}(S))=\operatorname{conv}(P(S))\). Hence projection alone causes no convex-hull loss when the lifted hull is exact. For an outer approximation, however, \(P(Q)\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(P(S))\), and the containment is strict exactly when there exists \(x\in P(Q)\setminus\operatorname{conv}(P(S))\). Any such point can be separated from the closed projected hull by a linear objective, producing a strictly weaker projected lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convexification survives linear projection. Projection loss occurs only when an inexact lifted relaxation projects to points outside the original-space convex hull.
assumptions_latex: The set \(\operatorname{conv}(P(S))\) is closed when separation is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(Q)\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(P(S))\), with strict relaxation loss precisely when the set difference is nonempty.

children.title: Unfavorable Algebraic Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Weakness caused by poor product groupings, DC decompositions, or primitive selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Unfavorable Algebraic Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation strength is ordered by containment of decomposition-induced lifted feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two algebraically equivalent decompositions of the same optimization model produce convex lifted relaxations \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\), expressed in a common lifted space after adding redundant coordinates if necessary. If \(Q_1\subseteq Q_2\), then for every common minimization objective \(c^{\mathsf T}z\), \(\inf_{z\in Q_1}c^{\mathsf T}z\ge\inf_{z\in Q_2}c^{\mathsf T}z\). Thus a product grouping, difference-of-convex decomposition, or primitive selection is unfavorable whenever it yields the larger relaxation. If the containment is strict and the sets are closed and convex, some linear objective separates the excess portion and makes the bound strictly worse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among equivalent decompositions, the one producing the larger convex feasible set gives no stronger lower bound and is strictly worse for some objective.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are valid convex relaxations of algebraically equivalent models.
Both relaxations use a common lifted coordinate space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_1\subseteq Q_2\) implies \(\inf_{Q_1}c^{\mathsf T}z\ge\inf_{Q_2}c^{\mathsf T}z\) for every common linear objective.

children.title: Computational Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Numerical and dimensional effects that undermine otherwise valid lower models.

children.title: Scale-Conditioning Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scaling effects on curvature estimation and convex-relaxation solution quality.

children.title: Variable-Scale Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Disparate variable magnitudes that degrade convex-relaxation representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Scale Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal coordinate scaling can create arbitrarily poor curvature conditioning in an otherwise well-conditioned model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) and the diagonal change of variables \(x=Dy\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) and every \(d_i>0\). In the original coordinates, \(\nabla^2 f=I\) and the spectral condition number is one. In the scaled coordinates, \(\nabla_y^2(f\circ D)=D^2\), so \(\kappa_2(D^2)=(\max_i d_i/\min_i d_i)^2\). Therefore an increasing scale ratio creates arbitrarily severe Hessian conditioning even though the underlying objective and minimizers are related by a bijective transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal variable scaling turns an identity Hessian into a matrix whose condition number is the square of the largest-to-smallest scale ratio.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
Conditioning is measured by the spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(\nabla_y^2(f\circ D))=(\max_i d_i/\min_i d_i)^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal-scaling calculation is standard and fits the leaf, but no source is supplied; an authoritative scaling or numerical-conditioning reference with a specific locator is required. The eventual sourced version should also state that the variables lie in \(\mathbb R^n\).

children.title: Curvature-Estimate Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of curvature information to scaling choices or numerical perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Estimate Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies underestimator degradation caused by conservative convexification curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on a box \(X=[l,u]\), and define the separable convexifying underestimator \(g_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(l_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\), where \(\alpha_i\ge0\) and \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) on \(X\). Then \(g_\alpha\) is convex and \(g_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\). If \(\alpha\) is replaced by a more conservative estimate \(\alpha+\Delta\alpha\), with \(\Delta\alpha\ge0\), the pointwise decrease is bounded by \(0\le g_\alpha(x)-g_{\alpha+\Delta\alpha}(x)\le\tfrac14\sum_i\Delta\alpha_i(u_i-l_i)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overestimating the curvature correction preserves validity but can lower the underestimator by one quarter of each excess coefficient times the squared box width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le g_\alpha-g_{\alpha+\Delta\alpha}\le\tfrac14\sum_i\Delta\alpha_i(u_i-l_i)^2\) pointwise on \(X\).

children.title: Relaxation Solver Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Poor numerical conditioning within convex underestimation subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Solver Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed stationarity tolerance loses objective accuracy as strong convexity vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unconstrained convex quadratic \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(H\succ0\), let \(x^*=H^{-1}b\). If a numerical relaxation solver returns \(\hat x\) satisfying \(\lVert\nabla q(\hat x)\rVert_2\le\tau\), then \(q(\hat x)-q(x^*)\le\tau^2/(2\lambda_{\min}(H))\). This estimate is attained when the residual is aligned with a minimum-eigenvalue eigenvector. Hence a fixed residual tolerance permits arbitrarily large objective error as \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\downarrow0\), even though the reported stationarity residual remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic, fixed gradient tolerance allows objective error proportional to the reciprocal of the smallest Hessian eigenvalue.
assumptions_latex: The solver termination test is \(\lVert\nabla q(\hat x)\rVert_2\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\hat x)-q(x^*)\le\tau^2/(2\lambda_{\min}(H))\), and this dependence is sharp.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic residual-to-objective-error bound and its sharp dependence on the smallest eigenvalue are mathematically credible, but the record has no inspectable numerical-conditioning source.

children.title: Scaling-Driven Bound Degradation
children.top_down_role: Loss of lower-bound quality attributable to unfavorable scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Driven Bound Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact affine reformulation preserves relaxation values; observed degradation identifies a non-invariant construction or numerical effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=Dy+d\) be a bijective affine scaling, and let \(Q_x\) be a convex relaxation with objective \(\phi_x(x)\). Define the exactly transformed relaxation \(Q_y=\{y:Dy+d\in Q_x\}\) and \(\phi_y(y)=\phi_x(Dy+d)\). Then \(\inf_{x\in Q_x}\phi_x(x)=\inf_{y\in Q_y}\phi_y(y)\). Therefore variable scaling alone cannot degrade an exact relaxation bound. A changed bound must arise because the relaxation was reconstructed non-equivariantly, parameters or stopping tolerances were not transformed consistently, finite-precision error intervened, or the variable map was not bijective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bijective affine rescaling preserves an exactly transformed relaxation bound; any observed change comes from construction, tolerance, precision, or noninvertibility effects.
assumptions_latex: The feasible relaxation and objective are transformed exactly under \(x=Dy+d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in Q_x}\phi_x(x)=\inf_{y\in Q_y}\phi_y(y)\).

notation.meaning: equivalent relaxations in original and scaled coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exact invariance under a bijective affine change of variables is correct and locally appropriate, but the record supplies no source for either the invariance statement or the listed mechanisms of observed degradation.

children.title: Lifted-Model Growth
children.top_down_role: Excessive auxiliary-variable, constraint, or conic representation size.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Model Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts lifted variables and constraints and isolates exponential growth from duplicated common subexpressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a factorable model represented by a directed acyclic graph with \(V\) noninput operation nodes and \(E\) operand arcs, a lift using one auxiliary variable per operation and a constant number of primitive constraints per arc has \(O(V)\) auxiliary variables and \(O(E)\) constraints. If common subexpressions are expanded into a tree instead of shared, these counts can be exponential in the graph depth. For example, the recurrence \(s_0=x\) and \(s_k=s_{k-1}s_{k-1}\) has a shared graph with \(k\) product nodes, whereas full syntactic expansion contains \(2^k-1\) product occurrences. Thus representation choice can dominate relaxation size before optimization begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared expression graph lifts linearly in graph size, while duplicating recursively reused subexpressions can create exponentially many auxiliaries and constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each operation receives one auxiliary variable.
Each operand arc generates at most a constant number of primitive constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Shared lifting has size \(O(V+E)\), while tree expansion can require \(\Theta(2^k)\) operation copies at depth \(k\).

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

children.title: Nonsmooth-Model Burden
children.top_down_role: Solver difficulties caused by recursively generated nonsmooth convex models.

assumptions_latex: At recursion depth \(k\), the convex lower model is \(m_k(x)=\max_{1\le i\le k}\{a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\}\) on a nonempty convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The model is retained explicitly, without eliminating redundant affine pieces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit model has \(k\) affine pieces, its epigraph formulation has \(k\) inequalities, and it is nondifferentiable at every point having distinct simultaneously active pieces.

notation.meaning: Recursive polyhedral convex underestimator after k pieces have been generated.
Feasible region on which the lower model is used.
Set of affine pieces active at x.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: maximum-of-affine representation and active-piece nonsmoothness are standard convex-analysis facts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral lower models formed by recursively accumulating affine cuts without redundancy removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k:X\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \[m_k(x)=\max_{1\le i\le k}\{a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\}.\] Its explicit epigraph representation is \[\operatorname{epi}_X(m_k)=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:t\ge a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\ \text{for every }i=1,\ldots,k\}.\] Hence retaining every generated piece makes the representation grow by one inequality per recursion. Moreover, if \(I_k(x)\) contains indices \(i\ne j\) with \(a_i\ne a_j\), then \(m_k\) is not differentiable at \(x\). The computational failure boundary is reached when this growing constrained nonsmooth model exceeds the size or regularity accepted by the designated lower-bound solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulating affine cuts enlarges the lower model linearly; ties between pieces create nondifferentiability. The approach fails computationally when model size or nonsmoothness exceeds solver capabilities.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth-Model Burden

However, the record cites no source for the claimed recursive computational burden or solver failure boundary. In addition, differentiability of a function declared only on an arbitrary convex set X is ambiguous at boundary points and on lower-dimensional X; the claim should either concern the ambient maximum-of-affine function on R^n or specify relative differentiability and sufficient conditions. The phrase 'exceeds the size or regularity accepted by the designated lower-bound solver' supplies no defined threshold or solver model. Source uncertainty and these scope issues make the proposed mathematical statement unreliable as written.

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), a baseline lower bound costs \(C_0(v)\), while a tighter convex-underestimation procedure costs \(C_1(v)\ge C_0(v)\).
Using the tighter bound changes the expected remaining search cost from \(R_0(v)\) to \(R_1(v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convex-underestimation effort is cost-dominated at \(v\) exactly when \(C_1(v)-C_0(v)\ge R_0(v)-R_1(v)\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compares incremental lower-bound cost with downstream computational savings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-node computational criterion for deciding when tighter convex bounds have negative net value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(v\), define the total expected computational work of method \(j\in\{0,1\}\) by \[T_j(v)=C_j(v)+R_j(v),\] where \(j=0\) is the baseline bound and \(j=1\) is a tighter convex underestimator. The tighter method is bound-cost dominated precisely when \[T_1(v)\ge T_0(v),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad C_1(v)-C_0(v)\ge R_0(v)-R_1(v).\] Thus its incremental construction-and-solution cost is at least the downstream work saved through stronger pruning or improved node selection. Strict inequality gives strictly greater expected work despite the tighter valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tighter lower bound is cost-dominated when its extra construction and solution cost is at least the downstream search work it saves.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the Bound-Cost Dominance container, and the displayed equivalence follows algebraically from the stipulated additive totals. Nevertheless, the record has no citation supporting this cost model as a recognized criterion for convex-underestimation regimes. The alleged exact boundary is effectively introduced by definition, while the meanings, conditioning, units, and estimation horizon of the expected downstream costs R_0(v) and R_1(v) are unspecified. A direct source or a clearly identified analytical cost-model framework is required before this can be retained as candidate-review knowledge.
